# Authentication

* API Key (meraki_api_key)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key**, in: header.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

- oAuth2 authentication. This API uses OAuth 2 with the authorization code grant flow. [More info](https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/api-v1/authorization/)

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://as.meraki.com/oauth/authorize](https://as.meraki.com/oauth/authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://as.meraki.com/oauth/token](https://as.meraki.com/oauth/token)

<h1 id="meraki-dashboard-api-organizations">organizations</h1>

## List the organizations that the user has privileges on

<a id="opIdgetOrganizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organizations`

List the organizations that the user has privileges on

<h3 id="list-the-organizations-that-the-user-has-privileges-on-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 9000. Default is 9000.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "2930418",
    "name": "My organization",
    "url": "https://dashboard.meraki.com/o/VjjsAd/manage/organization/overview",
    "api": {
      "enabled": true
    },
    "licensing": {
      "model": "co-term"
    },
    "cloud": {
      "region": {
        "name": "North America",
        "host": {
          "name": "United States"
        }
      }
    },
    "management": {
      "details": [
        {
          "name": "MSP ID",
          "value": "123456"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-the-organizations-that-the-user-has-privileges-on-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|» id|string|false|none|Organization ID|
|» name|string|false|none|Organization name|

## Create a new organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrganization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My organization",
    "management": {
      "details": [
        {
          "name": "MSP ID",
          "value": "123456"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

## Update an organization

## Return the list of action batches in the organization

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationActionBatches"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/actionBatches \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/actionBatches`

Return the list of action batches in the organization

<h3 id="return-the-list-of-action-batches-in-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 100.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sorted order of entries. Order options are 'ascending' and 'descending'. Default is 'ascending'.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter batches by status. Valid types are pending, completed, and failed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sortOrder|ascending|
|sortOrder|descending|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|
|status|pending|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "1234",
    "organizationId": "2930418",
    "confirmed": true,
    "synchronous": false,
    "status": {
      "completed": true,
      "failed": false,
      "errors": [],
      "createdResources": [
        {
          "id": "1284392014819",
          "uri": "/networks/L_XXXXX/groupPolicies/100"
        }
      ]
    },
    "actions": [
      {
        "resource": "/devices/QXXX-XXXX-XXXX/switch/ports/3",
        "operation": "update"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

<h3 id="return-the-list-of-action-batches-in-the-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-the-list-of-action-batches-in-the-organization-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|false|none|ID of the action batch. Can be used to check the status of the action batch at /organizations/{organizationId}/actionBatches/{actionBatchId}|
|» organizationId|string|false|none|ID of the organization this action batch belongs to|
|» confirmed|boolean|false|none|Flag describing whether the action should be previewed before executing or not|
|» synchronous|boolean|false|none|Flag describing whether actions should run synchronously or asynchronously|
|» status|object|false|none|Status of action batch|
|» » completed|boolean|false|none|Flag describing whether all actions in the action batch have completed|
|» » failed|boolean|false|none|Flag describing whether any actions in the action batch failed|
|» » errors|[string]|false|none|List of errors encountered when running actions in the action batch|
|» » createdResources|[object]|true|none|Resources created as a result of this action batch|
|» » » id|string|false|none|ID of the created resource|
|» » » uri|string|false|none|URI, not including base, of the created resource|
|» actions|[object]|true|none|A set of changes made as part of this action (<a href='https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/api/#/rest/guides/action-batches/'>more details</a>)|
|» » resource|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the resource to be acted on|
|» » operation|string|true|none|The operation to be used by this action|
|» » body|object|false|none|Data provided in the body of the Action. Contents depend on the Action type|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||A comma-separated list of first, last, prev, and next relative links used for subsequent paginated requests.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
meraki_api_key, bearerAuth
</aside>

## Create an action batch

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationActionBatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/actionBatches \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "confirmed": true,
    "synchronous": true,
    "actions": [
      {
        "resource": "/devices/QXXX-XXXX-XXXX/switch/ports/3",
        "operation": "create"
      }
    ],
    "callback": {
      "url": "https://webhook.site/28efa24e-f830-4d9f-a12b-fbb9e5035031",
      "sharedSecret": "secret",
      "httpServer": {
        "id": "aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZXhhbXBsZS5jb20vd2ViaG9va3M="
      },
      "payloadTemplate": {
        "id": "wpt_2100"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/actionBatches`

Create an action batch

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "confirmed": true,
  "synchronous": true,
  "actions": [
    {
      "resource": "/devices/QXXX-XXXX-XXXX/switch/ports/3",
      "operation": "create"
    }
```

## Creates new adaptive policy ACL

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationAdaptivePolicyAcl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/adaptivePolicy/acls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Block sensitive web traffic",
    "description": "Blocks sensitive web traffic",
    "rules": [
      {
        "policy": "deny",
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "srcPort": "1,33",
        "dstPort": "22-30",
        "log": true,
        "tcpEstablished": true
      }
    ],
    "ipVersion": "ipv6"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/adaptivePolicy/acls`

Creates new adaptive policy ACL

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Block sensitive web traffic",
  "description": "Blocks sensitive web traffic",
  "rules": [
    {
      "policy": "deny",
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "srcPort": "1,33",
      "dstPort": "22-30",
      "log": true,
      "tcpEstablished": true
    }
  ],
  "ipVersion": "ipv6"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-new-adaptive-policy-acl-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the adaptive policy ACL|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the adaptive policy ACL|
|» rules|body|[object]|true|An ordered array of the adaptive policy ACL rules.|
|» » policy|body|string|true|'allow' or 'deny' traffic specified by this rule.|
|» » protocol|body|string|true|The type of protocol (must be 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp' or 'any').|
|» » srcPort|body|string|false|Source port. Must be in the format of single port: '1', port list: '1,2' or port range: '1-10', and in the range of 1-65535, or 'any'. Default is 'any'.|
|» » dstPort|body|string|false|Destination port. Must be in the format of single port: '1', port list: '1,2' or port range: '1-10', and in the range of 1-65535, or 'any'. Default is 'any'.|
|» » log|body|boolean|false|If enabled, when this rule is hit an entry will be logged to the event log<br>|
|» » tcpEstablished|body|boolean|false|If enabled, means TCP connection with this node must be established.<br>Can only be enabled when policy protocol is 'allow tcp'<br>|
|» ipVersion|body|string|true|IP version of adpative policy ACL. One of: 'any', 'ipv4' or 'ipv6'|

|» ipVersion|ipv4|
|» ipVersion|ipv6|

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the adaptive policy ACL|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the adaptive policy ACL|
|» rules|body|[object]|false|An ordered array of the adaptive policy ACL rules. An empty array will clear the rules.|
|» » policy|body|string|true|'allow' or 'deny' traffic specified by this rule.|
|» » protocol|body|string|true|The type of protocol (must be 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp' or 'any').|
|» » srcPort|body|string|false|Source port. Must be in the format of single port: '1', port list: '1,2' or port range: '1-10', and in the range of 1-65535, or 'any'. Default is 'any'.|
|» » dstPort|body|string|false|Destination port. Must be in the format of single port: '1', port list: '1,2' or port range: '1-10', and in the range of 1-65535, or 'any'. Default is 'any'.|
|» » log|body|boolean|false|If enabled, when this rule is hit an entry will be logged to the event log<br>|
|» » tcpEstablished|body|boolean|false|If enabled, means TCP connection with this node must be established.<br>Can only be enabled when policy protocol is 'allow tcp'<br>|
|» ipVersion|body|string|false|IP version of adpative policy ACL. One of: 'any', 'ipv4' or 'ipv6'|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » policy|allow|
|» » policy|deny|
|» » protocol|any|
|» » protocol|icmp|
|» » protocol|tcp|
|» » protocol|udp|
|» ipVersion|any|
|» ipVersion|ipv4|
|» ipVersion|ipv6|

```json
  "description": "Blocks sensitive web traffic",
  "ipVersion": "ipv6",
  "rules": [
    {
      "policy": "deny",
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "srcPort": "1,33",
      "dstPort": "22-30",
      "log": true,
      "tcpEstablished": true
    }
  ],
  "createdAt": "2021-05-19T17:08:25Z",
  "updatedAt": "2021-05-19T17:11:54Z"
}
```

## List pipelines with operation and status metadata, sorted by pipeline ID

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationApiRestProvisioningPipelines"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/api/rest/provisioning/pipelines \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/api/rest/provisioning/pipelines`

List pipelines with operation and status metadata, sorted by pipeline ID. Pipeline IDs are assigned in creation order, so newer pipelines are returned first by default; sortOrder controls that ID order. Optional status and timespan filtering can limit the result set.

<h3 id="list-pipelines-with-operation-and-status-metadata-sorted-by-pipeline-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 100. Default is 10.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sorted order of entries. Order options are 'ascending' and 'descending'. Default is 'descending'.|
|status|query|string|false|If provided, filters pipelines by status. If omitted, pipelines of all statuses are returned. `pending` pipelines have not started, `active` pipelines have started but not finished, `success` pipelines completed successfully, and `error` pipelines failed.|
|timespan|query|integer|false|Created-at lookback for matching pipelines, in seconds. Defaults to 7200 seconds. The maximum is 30 days.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sortOrder|ascending|
|sortOrder|descending|
|status|active|
|status|error|
|status|pending|
|status|success|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "pipelineId": "1234",
      "operation": {
        "id": "enrollOrganizationSaseSites"
      },
      "status": "active"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "counts": {
      "items": {
        "total": 100,
        "remaining": 10
      }
    }
```

## Return all health alerts for an organization

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/assurance/alerts`

Return all health alerts for an organization

<h3 id="return-all-health-alerts-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 4 - 300. Default is 30.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sorted order of entries. Order options are 'ascending' and 'descending'. Default is 'ascending'.|
|networkId|query|string|false|Optional parameter to filter alerts by network ids.|
|severity|query|string|false|Optional parameter to filter by severity type.|
|types|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter by alert type.|
|tsStart|query|string(date-time)|false|Optional parameter to filter by starting timestamp|
|tsEnd|query|string(date-time)|false|Optional parameter to filter by end timestamp|
|category|query|string|false|Optional parameter to filter by category.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|Optional parameter to set column to sort by.|
|serials|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter by primary device serial|
|deviceTypes|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter by device types|
|deviceTags|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter by device tags|

|dismissed|query|boolean|false|Optional parameter to filter by dismissed alerts defaults to false|
|resolved|query|boolean|false|Optional parameter to filter by resolved alerts defaults to false|
|suppressAlertsForOfflineNodes|query|boolean|false|When set to true the api will only return connectivity alerts for a given device if that device is in an offline state. ## Dismiss health alerts

<a id="opIddismissOrganizationAssuranceAlerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/assurance/alerts/dismiss \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "alertIds": [
      "1234",
      "4567"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/assurance/alerts/dismiss`

Dismiss health alerts

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alertIds": [
    "1234",
    "4567"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="dismiss-health-alerts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» alertIds|body|[string]|true|Array of alert IDs in this organization to dismiss. Missing or inaccessible alert IDs return 404.|

<h3 id="dismiss-health-alerts-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Successful operation|None|

meraki_api_key, bearerAuth

<h3 id="return-a-summary-of-alerts-grouped-by-type-and-severity-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|items|[object]|true|none|Organization Alert counts by type|
|» type|string|true|none|Alert Type|
|» categoryType|string|true|none|Alert category|
|» severity|string|true|none|Alert severity|
|» lastAlertedAt|string(date-time)|true|none|Last time an alert of this type was triggered|
|» lastResolvedAt|string(date-time)|false|none|Last time an alert of this type was resolved|
|» count|integer|true|none|Total count of the given alert type|
|» networkCount|integer|true|none|Number of affected networks for the alert type|
|» deviceTypes|[string]|true|none|Affected device types for alerts in the group|
|» deviceTags|[string]|true|none|Unique device tags for alerts in the group|
|» networks|[object]|true|none|Affected networks for alerts in the group|
|» » id|string|true|none|Network identifier|
|» » name|string|true|none|Network name|
|meta|object|true|none|Metadata about the response|
|» counts|object|true|none|Counts|
|» » items|integer|true|none|Total Alerts|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||A comma-separated list of first, last, prev, and next relative links used for subsequent paginated requests.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: dashboard:general:telemetry:read )
</aside>

## Returns historical health alert overviews

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationAssuranceAlertsOverviewHistorical"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/assurance/alerts/overview/historical?segmentDuration=0&tsStart=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/assurance/alerts/overview/historical`

Returns historical health alert overviews

<h3 id="returns-historical-health-alert-overviews-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|segmentDuration|query|integer|true|Amount of time in seconds for each segment in the returned dataset|
|networkId|query|string|false|Optional parameter to filter alerts overview by network ids.|
|severity|query|string|false|Optional parameter to filter alerts overview by severity type.|
|types|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter by alert type.|
|tsStart|query|string(date-time)|true|Parameter to define starting timestamp of historical totals|
|tsEnd|query|string(date-time)|false|Optional parameter to filter by end timestamp defaults to the current time|
|category|query|string|false|Optional parameter to filter by category.|
|serials|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter by primary device serial|
|deviceTypes|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter by device types|

## Add a new branding policy to an organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationBrandingPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/brandingPolicies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My Branding Policy",
    "enabled": true,
    "appearance": {
      "dashboardMenuTheme": "light"
    },
    "adminSettings": {
      "appliesTo": "All admins of networks...",
      "values": [
        "N_1234",
        "L_5678"
      ]
    },
    "helpSettings": {
      "helpTab": "show",
      "getHelpSubtab": "default or inherit",
      "communitySubtab": "show",
      "casesSubtab": "hide",
      "dataProtectionRequestsSubtab": "default or inherit",
      "getHelpSubtabKnowledgeBaseSearch": "<h1>Some custom HTML content</h1>",
      "universalSearchKnowledgeBaseSearch": "hide",
      "ciscoMerakiProductDocumentation": "show",
      "supportContactInfo": "show",
      "newFeaturesSubtab": "show",
      "firewallInfoSubtab": "hide",
      "apiDocsSubtab": "default or inherit",
      "hardwareReplacementsSubtab": "hide",
      "smForums": "hide",
      "helpWidget": "hide"
    },
    "customLogo": {
      "enabled": true,
      "image": {
        "contents": "Hyperg26C8F4h8CvcoUqpA==",
        "format": "jpg"
      }
    }
  }'
```

## Return the branding policy IDs of an organization in priority order

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationBrandingPoliciesPriorities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/brandingPolicies/priorities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/brandingPolicies/priorities`

Return the branding policy IDs of an organization in priority order. IDs are ordered in ascending order of priority (IDs later in the array have higher priority).

<h3 id="return-the-branding-policy-ids-of-an-organization-in-priority-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "brandingPolicyIds": [
    "123",
    "456",
    "789"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="return-the-branding-policy-ids-of-an-organization-in-priority-order-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-the-branding-policy-ids-of-an-organization-in-priority-order-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|brandingPolicyIds|[string]|false|none|      An ordered list of branding policy IDs that determines the priority order of how to apply the policies<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: dashboard:iam:config:read )
</aside>

## List certificate authorities for an organization

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationCertificatesAuthorities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/certificates/authorities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/certificates/authorities`

List certificate authorities for an organization. Optionally filter by authority IDs and sort results.

<h3 id="list-certificate-authorities-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|authorityIds|query|[string]|false|Feature certificate authority IDs to filter by (exact match on each id; duplicates are ignored)|
|sortBy|query|string|false|Field to sort by (default: authorityId)|
|direction|query|string|false|Sort direction (default: asc)|
|includeChain|query|boolean|false|When true, include the certification path from each certificate authority up to the self signed root. Required by validators that cannot anchor trust at a non self signed certificate authority. Defaults to false.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 100. Default is 50.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sortBy|authorityId|
|sortBy|featureType|
|sortBy|status|
|direction|asc|
|direction|desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "authority": {
        "id": "5409",
        "name": "radsec-123"
      },
      "feature": {
        "type": "radsec"
      },
      "status": "untrusted",
      "contents": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\\n...\\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\\n",
      "chain": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\\n...\\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\\n-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\\n...\\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\\n"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "counts": {
      "items": {
        "total": 2,
        "remaining": 0
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-certificate-authorities-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="list-certificate-authorities-for-an-organization-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|items|[object]|false|none|Certificate authorities|
|» authority|object|false|none|Certificate authority reference|
|» » id|string|false|none|Unique ID of the certificate authority|
|» » name|string|false|none|Certificate authority name|
|» feature|object|false|none|Feature context for this certificate authority|
|» » type|string|false|none|Feature type|
|» status|string|false|none|Feature certificate authority lifecycle state: untrusted (new), trusted (in use), revoked, or pending_revoked (revocation in progress).|
|» contents|string|false|none|PEM encoded certificate authority contents with newlines as \n; null if not generated|
|» chain|string|false|none|PEM bundle of the complete certification path, ordered from this certificate authority up to the self signed root, with newlines as \n. Only returned when includeChain is true. If a complete path is unavailable for any certificate authority in the response, the request fails rather than returning a partial path.|
|meta|object|false|none|Metadata about returned items|
|» counts|object|false|none|Result counts|
|» » items|object|false|none|Item counts|
|» » » total|integer|false|none|Total number of items returned|
|» » » remaining|integer|false|none|Remaining items (always 0)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|openroaming|
|» » type|radsec|
|» » type|zigbee|
|» status|pending_revoked|
|» status|revoked|
|» status|trusted|
|» status|untrusted|

```bash
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/claim`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Claim a list of devices, licenses, and/or orders into an organization inventory. When claiming by order, all devices and licenses in the order will be claimed; licenses will be added to the organization and devices will be placed in the organization's inventory. This operation can be used up to ten times within a single five minute window.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "orders": [
    "4CXXXXXXX"
  ],
  "serials": [
    "Q234-ABCD-5678"
  ],
  "licenses": [
    {
      "key": "Z2XXXXXXXXXX",
      "mode": "addDevices"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="claim-a-list-of-devices-licenses-andor-orders-into-an-organization-inventory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» orders|body|[string]|false|The numbers of the orders that should be claimed|
|» serials|body|[string]|false|The serials of the devices that should be claimed|
|» licenses|body|[object]|false|The licenses that should be claimed|
|» » key|body|string|true|The key of the license|
|» » mode|body|string|false|Either 'renew' or 'addDevices'. 'addDevices' will increase the license limit, while 'renew' will extend the amount of time until expiration. Defaults to 'addDevices'. All licenses must be claimed with the same mode, and at most one renewal can be claimed at a time. This parameter is legacy and does not apply to organizations with per-device licensing enabled.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » mode|addDevices|
|» » mode|renew|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "orders": [
    "4CXXXXXXX"
  ],
  "serials": [
    "Q234-ABCD-5678"
  ],
  "licenses": [
    {
      "key": "Z2XXXXXXXXXX",
      "mode": "addDevices"
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/cellular/data/profiles`

```json
            "dayOfWeek": "mon",
            "dayOfMonth": 2
          }
        }
      },
      "actions": [
        {
          "type": "failover"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» » slot|body|string|true|The logical SIM identifier that the rule is applied to. One of: 'sim1', 'sim2', or 'esim'. Devices included in this group must have an active card/profile with the defined SIM slot in order to use this rule.|
|» » uplink|body|object|true|Configuration for the uplink governed by this rule.|
|» » » priority|body|integer|true|The uplink priority for this rule. One of: 1 or 2, where 1 is the highest priority.|
|» » » isPreferred|body|boolean|true|Whether this uplink is the preferred one to use once all rules have been exhausted.|
|» » cap|body|object|true|The data cap values to be set with this rule.|
|» » » value|body|integer|true|The total bandwidth available for the specified term in megabytes.|
|» » » threshold|body|number(float)|false|The data usage threshold at which the rule should be triggered. This is expressed as a float between 0.01 and 1.0 (where 0.01 is equal to 1% of total and 1.0 is equal to 100%). By default this will be 1.0.|
|» » » term|body|object|true|The data usage term configuration that determines when the aggregated data count resets on the device.|

## List Cellular Data Management Profile assignments in this organization

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationDevicesCellularDataProfilesAssignments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/devices/cellular/data/profiles/assignments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/cellular/data/profiles/assignments`

List Cellular Data Management Profile assignments in this organization. Returns paginated device-to-profile assignments and supports filtering by profile IDs and device serials.

<h3 id="list-cellular-data-management-profile-assignments-in-this-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|profileIds|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to find assignments by Profile IDs. Maximum 1000 profile IDs.|
|serials|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to find assignments by Device Serials. Maximum 1000 serials.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 100.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "assignmentId": "42",
      "profile": {
        "id": "1234"
      },
      "device": {
        "serial": "Q234-ABCD-5678"
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "counts": {
      "items": {
        "total": 1,
        "remaining": 0
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-cellular-data-management-profile-assignments-in-this-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="list-cellular-data-management-profile-assignments-in-this-organization-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|items|[object]|false|none|List of Cellular Data Management Profile device assignments. Maximum 1000 assignments per page.|
|» assignmentId|string|false|none|Unique ID of the device assignment|
|» profile|object|false|none|Profile assigned to the device|
|» » id|string|false|none|ID of the profile the device was assigned to|
|» device|object|false|none|Device assigned to the profile|
|» » serial|string|false|none|Serial of the device assigned|
|meta|object|false|none|Meta data about the results|
|» counts|object|false|none|Counts of involved entities|
|» » items|object|false|none|Count of Cellular Data Management Profile device assignments.|
|» » » total|integer|false|none|Total number of Cellular Data Management Profile device assignments available.|
|» » » remaining|integer|false|none|Remaining number of Cellular Data Management Profile device assignments available for pagination.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||A comma-separated list of first, last, prev, and next relative links used for subsequent paginated requests.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: sdwan:config:read )
</aside>

|» » device|body|object|true|Device to assign to the profile|


`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/cellular/data/usage/history/byDevice/byInterval`

List historical cellular data usage grouped by device and interval in this organization. Returns a paginated per-device time series with per-SIM totals and supports the standard t0, t1, timespan, and interval query parameters.

<h3 id="list-historical-cellular-data-usage-grouped-by-device-and-interval-in-this-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|serials|query|[string]|true|Required parameter to filter the results by device serials. Maximum 10 serials.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 10. Default is 5.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 366 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day. If interval is provided, the timespan will be autocalculated.|
|interval|query|integer|false|The time interval in seconds for returned data. The valid intervals are: 300, 1200, 14400, 86400. The default is 86400. Interval is calculated if time params are provided.|

```json
            "total": 1234,

            ]

        }
      ]

    "counts": {

        "total": 1,
        "remaining": 0
      }
    }

}
```

## List Packet Captures

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationDevicesPacketCaptureCaptures"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/devices/packetCapture/captures \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/packetCapture/captures`

List Packet Captures. The current license level allows storage of up to 10 capture files in the cloud. When this limit is reached and a new capture is taken, the oldest capture will be automatically deleted to ensure sufficient space. Additional storage for switches will be available with an advantage license at a future date. These future capabilities will be consistent with what is available today via advantage licensing for access points.

<h3 id="list-packet-captures-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|captureIds|query|[string]|false|Return the packet captures of the specified capture ids|
|networkIds|query|[string]|false|Return the packet captures of the specified network(s)|
|serials|query|[string]|false|Return the packet captures of the specified device(s)|
|process|query|[string]|false|Return the packet captures of the specified process|
|captureStatus|query|[string]|false|Return the packet captures of the specified capture status|
|name|query|[string]|false|Return the packet captures matching the specified name|
|clientMac|query|[string]|false|Return the packet captures matching the specified client macs|
|notes|query|string|false|Return the packet captures matching the specified notes|
|deviceName|query|string|false|Return the packet captures matching the specified device name|
|adminName|query|string|false|Return the packet captures matching the admin name|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 365 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 365 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 365 days. The default is 365 days.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 100. Default is 10.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sorted order of entries. Order options are 'ascending' and 'descending'. Default is 'descending'.|

## Perform a packet capture on a device and store in Meraki Cloud

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationDevicesPacketCaptureCapture"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/devices/packetCapture/captures \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "serials": [
      "Q234-ABCD-5678"
    ],
    "name": "Capture no. 3",
    "outputType": "upload_to_cloud",
    "destination": "upload_to_cloud",
    "ports": "1, 3",
    "notes": "Debugging connectivity issue...",
    "duration": 3,
    "filterExpression": "host 10.1.27.253",
    "interface": "wireless",
    "advanced": {
      "physicalInterfaceDirection": "both",
      "controlPlaneDirection": "both",
      "innerFilterMacs": [
        "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff",
        "11:22:33:44:55:66"
      ],
      "bufferFiles": 5,
      "maxFilesize": 10,
      "captureType": "circular",
      "packetsPerSecond": 10000
    }
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/packetCapture/captures`

Perform a packet capture on a device and store in Meraki Cloud. Only a single switch may be chosen per request, while multiple access points are allowed at once.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "serials": [
    "Q234-ABCD-5678"
  ],
  "name": "Capture no. 3",
  "outputType": "upload_to_cloud",
  "destination": "upload_to_cloud",
  "ports": "1, 3",
  "notes": "Debugging connectivity issue...",
  "duration": 3,
  "filterExpression": "host 10.1.27.253",
  "interface": "wireless",
  "advanced": {
    "physicalInterfaceDirection": "both",
    "controlPlaneDirection": "both",
    "innerFilterMacs": [
      "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff",
      "11:22:33:44:55:66"
    ],
    "bufferFiles": 5,
    "maxFilesize": 10,
    "captureType": "circular",
    "packetsPerSecond": 10000
  }
}
```

<h3 id="perform-a-packet-capture-on-a-device-and-store-in-meraki-cloud-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» serials|body|[string]|true|The serial(s) of the device(s)|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of packet capture file|
|» outputType|body|string|false|Output type of packet capture file. Possible values: text, pcap, cloudshark, or upload_to_cloud|
|» destination|body|string|false|Destination of packet capture file. Possible values: [upload_to_cloud]|
|» ports|body|string|false|Ports of packet capture file, comma-separated|
|» notes|body|string|false|Reason for taking the packet capture|
|» duration|body|integer|false|Duration in seconds of packet capture|
|» filterExpression|body|string|false|Filter expression for packet capture|
|» interface|body|string|false|Interface of the device|
|» advanced|body|object|false|Advanced filters for IOSXE devices (supported for Campus Gateway devices only)|
|» » physicalInterfaceDirection|body|string|false|Direction for physical interface capture|
|» » controlPlaneDirection|body|string|false|Direction for control plane capture|
|» » innerFilterMacs|body|[string]|false|Inner MAC address filter for tunneled traffic (up to 5 MAC addresses for Campus Gateway devices)|
|» » bufferFiles|body|integer|false|Number of buffer files for circular buffer capture (1-5 for Campus Gateway devices)|
|» » maxFilesize|body|integer|false|Maximum file size in megabytes (MB). Range: 1-100 MB when bufferFiles=1, 1-500 MB when bufferFiles=2-5|
|» » captureType|body|string|false|Type of capture. Possible values: linear (default), circular|
|» » packetsPerSecond|body|integer|false|Packets per second limit for Campus Gateway devices (1-1000000).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » physicalInterfaceDirection|both|
|» » physicalInterfaceDirection|in|
|» » physicalInterfaceDirection|out|
|» » controlPlaneDirection|both|
|» » controlPlaneDirection|in|
|» » controlPlaneDirection|out|

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "captureId": "1234",
  "network": {
    "id": "N_24329156",
    "name": "Main Office"
  },
  "device": {
    "name": "My AP",
    "serial": "Q234-ABCD-5678"
  },
  "admin": {
    "id": "1234",
    "name": "Miles Meraki"
```

## Perform a packet capture on multiple devices and store in Meraki Cloud.

<a id="opIdbulkOrganizationDevicesPacketCaptureCapturesCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/devices/packetCapture/captures/bulkCreate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "devices": [
      {
        "serial": "Q234-ABCD-5678",
        "switchports": "1, 2",
        "interface": "TenGigabitEthernet0/0/0"
      }
    ],
    "notes": "Debugging persistent issue on device",
    "duration": 60,
    "filterExpression": "(icmp)",
    "name": "Capture no. 3",
    "advanced": {
      "physicalInterfaceDirection": "both",
      "controlPlaneDirection": "both",
      "innerFilterMac": [
        "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff",
        "11:22:33:44:55:66"
      ],
      "bufferFiles": 5,
      "maxFilesize": 10,
      "captureType": "circular"
    }
  }'
```

## Return the uplink loss and latency for every MX in the organization from at latest 2 minutes ago

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationDevicesUplinksLossAndLatency"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/devices/uplinksLossAndLatency \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/uplinksLossAndLatency`

Return the uplink loss and latency for every MX in the organization from at latest 2 minutes ago

<h3 id="return-the-uplink-loss-and-latency-for-every-mx-in-the-organization-from-at-latest-2-minutes-ago-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 60 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 5 minutes after t0. The latest possible time that t1 can be is 2 minutes into the past.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 5 minutes. The default is 5 minutes.|
|uplink|query|string|false|Optional filter for a specific WAN uplink. Valid uplinks are wan1, wan2, wan3, cellular. Default will return all uplinks.|
|ip|query|string|false|Optional filter for a specific destination IP. Default will return all destination IPs.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|uplink|cellular|
|uplink|wan1|
|uplink|wan2|
|uplink|wan3|

## Claim a list of devices, licenses, and/or orders into an organization inventory

<a id="opIdclaimIntoOrganizationInventory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/inventory/claim \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "orders": [
      "4CXXXXXXX"
    ],
    "serials": [
      "Q234-ABCD-5678"
    ],
    "licenses": [
      {
        "key": "Z2XXXXXXXXXX",
        "mode": "addDevices"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/inventory/claim`

Claim a list of devices, licenses, and/or orders into an organization inventory. When claiming by order, all devices and licenses in the order will be claimed; licenses will be added to the organization and devices will be placed in the organization's inventory. This operation can be used up to ten times within a single five minute window.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "orders": [
    "4CXXXXXXX"
  ],
  "serials": [
    "Q234-ABCD-5678"
  ],
  "licenses": [
    {
      "key": "Z2XXXXXXXXXX",
      "mode": "addDevices"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="claim-a-list-of-devices-licenses-andor-orders-into-an-organization-inventory-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» orders|body|[string]|false|The numbers of the orders that should be claimed|
|» serials|body|[string]|false|The serials of the devices that should be claimed|
|» licenses|body|[object]|false|The licenses that should be claimed|
|» » key|body|string|true|The key of the license|
|» » mode|body|string|false|Co-term licensing only: either 'renew' or 'addDevices'. 'addDevices' will increase the license limit, while 'renew' will extend the amount of time until expiration. Defaults to 'addDevices'. All licenses must be claimed with the same mode, and at most one renewal can be claimed at a time. Does not apply to organizations using per-device licensing model.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » mode|addDevices|
|» » mode|renew|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "orders": [
    "4CXXXXXXX"
  ],
  "serials": [
    "Q234-ABCD-5678"
  ],
  "licenses": [
    {
      "key": "Z2XXXXXXXXXX",
      "mode": "addDevices"
    }
  ]
}
```

|search|query|string|false|Search for devices in inventory based on serial number, mac address, or model.|
|macs|query|[string]|false|Search for devices in inventory based on mac addresses.|
|networkIds|query|[string]|false|Search for devices in inventory based on network ids. Use explicit 'null' value to get available devices only.|

List the licenses for an organization

<h3 id="list-the-licenses-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 1000.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|deviceSerial|query|string|false|Filter the licenses to those assigned to a particular device. Returned in the same order that they are queued to the device.|
|networkId|query|string|false|Filter the licenses to those assigned in a particular network|
|state|query|string|false|Filter the licenses to those in a particular state. Can be one of 'active', 'expired', 'expiring', 'recentlyQueued', 'unused' or 'unusedActive'|

|» ipRestrictionsForKeys|object|false|none|Details for API-only IP restrictions.|
|» » enabled|boolean|false|none|Boolean indicating whether the organization will restrict API key (not Dashboard GUI) usage to a specific list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges.|
|» » ranges|[string]|false|none|List of acceptable IP ranges. Entries can be single IP addresses, IP address ranges, and CIDR subnets.|

## List the networks that the user has privileges on in an organization

```bash

```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/networks`

List the networks that the user has privileges on in an organization

<h3 id="list-the-networks-that-the-user-has-privileges-on-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|configTemplateId|query|string|false|An optional parameter that is the ID of a config template. Will return all networks bound to that template.|
|isBoundToConfigTemplate|query|boolean|false|An optional parameter to filter config template bound networks. If configTemplateId is set, this cannot be false.|
|tags|query|[string]|false|An optional parameter to filter networks by tags. The filtering is case-sensitive. If tags are included, 'tagsFilterType' should also be included (see below).|
|tagsFilterType|query|string|false|An optional parameter of value 'withAnyTags' or 'withAllTags' to indicate whether to return networks which contain ANY or ALL of the included tags. If no type is included, 'withAnyTags' will be selected.|
|productTypes|query|[string]|false|An optional parameter to filter networks by product type. Results will have at least one of the included product types.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 100000. Default is 1000.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/networks/moves`

Move networks from one organization to another. Cross-shard moves must be enabled for your organization. For more information and caveats around network move limitations see the Network Portability documentation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "network": {
    "id": "N_569142402909112097"
  },
  "organizations": {
    "target": {
      "id": "146308"
    }

  "simulate": false
}
```

|» » target|body|object|true|The organization to which the network is moving|

## Create an Organization-Wide Policy Firewall Rule

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationPoliciesGlobalFirewallRulesetsRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/policies/global/firewall/rulesets/rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Allow developers",
    "rulesetId": "32",
    "policy": "deny",
    "enabled": true,
    "priority": 100,
    "description": "This is rule 1",
    "logging": {
      "enabled": false
    },
    "sources": {
      "matchCriteria": [
        "addressRanges",
        "ports",
        "policyObjects",
        "policyObjectGroups",
        "applianceVlans"
      ],
      "criteria": {
        "addressRanges": [
          "1.1.1.1",
          "2.2.2.2"
        ],
        "ports": [
          "22",
          "42-46"
        ],
        "policyObjects": [
          {
            "id": "23"
          }
        ],
        "policyObjectGroups": [
          {
            "id": "45"
          }
        ],
        "applianceVlans": [
          {
            "interfaceId": "L_123456789012345678_vlan_200"
          }
        ],
        "siteSpecificVlans": [
          {
            "id": 100,
            "address": {
              "offsets": {
                "ipv4": 25,
                "ipv6": "0:ff:fe01:0"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    "destinations": {
      "matchCriteria": [
        "addressRanges",
        "services",
        "applicationCategories",
        "applications",
        "policyObjects",
        "policyObjectGroups",
        "applianceVlans"
      ],
      "criteria": {
        "addressRanges": [
          "1.1.1.1",
          "2.2.2.2"
        ],
        "ports": [
          "22",
          "42-46"
        ],
        "services": [
          {
            "protocol": "tcp",
            "ports": [
              "80",
              "443"
            ]
          }
        ],
        "applicationCategories": [
          {
            "id": "meraki:layer7/category/24",
            "name": "Advertising",
            "applications": [
              {
                "id": "meraki:layer7/application/5",
                "name": "Advertising.com"
              }
            ]
          }
        ],
        "applications": [
          {
            "id": "meraki:layer7/application/5",
            "name": "Advertising.com"
          }
        ],
        "policyObjects": [
          {
            "id": "23"
          }
        ],
        "policyObjectGroups": [
          {
            "id": "45"
          }
        ],
        "adaptivePolicyGroups": [
          {
            "id": "123"
          }
        ],
        "applianceVlans": [
          {
            "interfaceId": "L_123456789012345678_vlan_200"
          }
        ],
        "countries": [
          {
            "code": "US"
          }
        ],
        "fqdns": [
          "*.example.com"
        ],
        "siteSpecificVlans": [
          {
            "id": 100,
            "address": {
              "offsets": {
                "ipv4": 25,
                "ipv6": "0:ff:fe01:0"
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

<h3 id="create-an-organization-wide-policy-firewall-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the firewall rule|
|» rulesetId|body|string|true|Firewall ruleset ID to associate the rule with|
|» policy|body|string|true|Rule policy - allow or deny traffic|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the rule is enabled|
|» priority|body|integer|false|Rule priority (lower numbers = higher priority)|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the firewall rule|
|» logging|body|object|false|Logging settings for the rule|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether logging is enabled for traffic matching this rule|

|» » matchCriteria|body|[string]|true|Source match criteria types|
|» » criteria|body|object|false|Source criteria values (not present if 'any' is in matchCriteria)|
|» » » addressRanges|body|[string]|false|Address ranges or addresses|

For IPv6, the offset forms the interface identifier suffix appended to the /64 prefix (e.g., prefix 2001:db8::/64 + offset 'ff:fe01' = 2001:db8::ff:fe01).|

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/sase/sites/attach`

Attach sites in this organization to Secure Access. For an organization, a maximum of 2500 sites can be attached if they are in spoke mode or a maximum of 100 sites can be attached in hub mode.

```json
    {
```

## Update a network

<a id="opIdupdateNetwork"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Main Office",
    "timeZone": "America/Los_Angeles",
    "tags": [
      "tag1",
      "tag2"
    ],
    "enrollmentString": "my-enrollment-string",
    "notes": "Additional description of the network"
  }'
```

`PUT /networks/{networkId}`

Update a network

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Main Office",
  "timeZone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "tags": [
    "tag1",
    "tag2"
  ],
  "enrollmentString": "my-enrollment-string",
  "notes": "Additional description of the network"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the network|

## List the clients that have used this network in the timespan

<a id="opIdgetNetworkClients"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/clients \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/clients`

List the clients that have used this network in the timespan. The data is updated at most once every five minutes.

<h3 id="list-the-clients-that-have-used-this-network-in-the-timespan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameter t0. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 5000. Default is 10.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|statuses|query|[string]|false|Filters clients based on status. Can be one of 'Online' or 'Offline'.|
|ip|query|string|false|Filters clients based on a partial or full match for the ip address field.|
|ip6|query|string|false|Filters clients based on a partial or full match for the ip6 address field.|
|ip6Local|query|string|false|Filters clients based on a partial or full match for the ip6Local address field.|
|mac|query|string|false|Filters clients based on a partial or full match for the mac address field.|
|os|query|string|false|Filters clients based on a partial or full match for the os (operating system) field.|
|pskGroup|query|string|false|Filters clients based on partial or full match for the iPSK name field.|
|description|query|string|false|Filters clients based on a partial or full match for the description field.|
|vlan|query|string|false|Filters clients based on the full match for the VLAN field.|
|namedVlan|query|string|false|Filters clients based on the partial or full match for the named VLAN field.|
|recentDeviceConnections|query|[string]|false|Filters clients based on recent connection type. Can be one of 'Wired' or 'Wireless'.|

#### Enumerated Values

## Return the usage histories for clients

<a id="opIdgetNetworkClientsUsageHistories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/clients/usageHistories?clients=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/clients/usageHistories`

Return the usage histories for clients. Usage data is in kilobytes. Clients can be identified by client keys or either the MACs or IPs depending on whether the network uses Track-by-IP.

<h3 id="return-the-usage-histories-for-clients-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|clients|query|string|true|A list of client keys, MACs or IPs separated by comma.|
|ssidNumber|query|integer|false|An SSID number to include. If not specified, events for all SSIDs will be returned.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|ssidNumber|0|
|ssidNumber|1|
|ssidNumber|2|
|ssidNumber|3|
|ssidNumber|4|
|ssidNumber|5|
|ssidNumber|6|
|ssidNumber|7|
|ssidNumber|8|
|ssidNumber|9|
|ssidNumber|10|
|ssidNumber|11|
|ssidNumber|12|
|ssidNumber|13|
|ssidNumber|14|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "clientId": "k74272e",
    "clientIp": "1.2.3.4",
    "clientMac": "00:11:22:33:44:55",
    "usageHistory": [
      {
        "received": 61,
        "sent": 138,
        "ts": "2018-02-11T00:00:00.090210Z"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

<h3 id="return-the-usage-histories-for-clients-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-the-usage-histories-for-clients-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» clientId|string|false|none|The identifier of the client|
|» clientIp|string|false|none|The IP address of the client|
|» clientMac|string|false|none|The MAC address of the client|
|» usageHistory|[object]|false|none|An array of usage history records for the client|
|» » received|number(float)|false|none|Usage received by the client on a given day|
|» » sent|number(float)|false|none|Usage sent by the client on a given day|
|» » ts|string(date-time)|false|none|The day's timestamp|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||A comma-separated list of first, last, prev, and next relative links used for subsequent paginated requests.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

## Return the client's network traffic data over time

<a id="opIdgetNetworkClientTrafficHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/clients/string/trafficHistory \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/clients/{clientId}/trafficHistory`

Return the client's network traffic data over time. Usage data is in kilobytes. This endpoint requires detailed traffic analysis to be enabled on the Network-wide > General page. Clients can be identified by a client key or either the MAC or IP depending on whether the network uses Track-by-IP.

<h3 id="return-the-clients-network-traffic-data-over-time-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|clientId|path|string|true|Client ID|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "ts": "2018-02-11T00:00:00.090210Z",
    "application": "Google",
    "destination": "www.google.com",
    "protocol": "TCP",
    "port": 443,
    "recv": 61,
    "sent": 138,
    "numFlows": 5,
    "activeSeconds": 240
  }
]
```

<h3 id="return-the-clients-network-traffic-data-over-time-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-the-clients-network-traffic-data-over-time-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» ts|string(date-time)|false|none|The start time from which daily traffic data was collected|
|» application|string|false|none|The name of the application the client is connected to|
|» destination|string|false|none|The IP or web address the client is connected to|
|» protocol|string|false|none|The client protocol|
|» port|integer|false|none|The port the client is connected to|
|» recv|number(float)|false|none|Usage received by the client|
|» sent|number(float)|false|none|Usage sent by the client|
|» numFlows|integer|false|none|The number of flows the client has|
|» activeSeconds|integer|false|none|The amount of seconds the client was active|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||A comma-separated list of first, last, prev, and next relative links used for subsequent paginated requests.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: dashboard:general:telemetry:read )
</aside>

## Claim devices into a network. (Note: for recently claimed devices, it may take a few minutes for API requests against that device to succeed)

<a id="opIdclaimNetworkDevices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/devices/claim \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "serials": [
      "Q234-ABCD-0001",
      "Q234-ABCD-0002",
      "Q234-ABCD-0003"
    ],
    "detailsByDevice": [
      {
        "serial": "Q234-ABCD-5678",
        "details": [
          {
            "name": "username",
            "value": "milesmeraki"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "addAtomically": true
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/devices/claim`

Claim devices into a network. (Note: for recently claimed devices, it may take a few minutes for API requests against that device to succeed). This operation can be used up to ten times within a single five minute window.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "serials": [
    "Q234-ABCD-0001",
    "Q234-ABCD-0002",
    "Q234-ABCD-0003"
  ],
  "detailsByDevice": [
    {
      "serial": "Q234-ABCD-5678",
      "details": [
        {
          "name": "username",
          "value": "milesmeraki"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "addAtomically": true
}
```

<h3 id="claim-devices-into-a-network-note-for-recently-claimed-devices-it-may-take-a-few-minutes-for-api-requests-against-that-device-to-succeed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|addAtomically|query|boolean|false|Whether to claim devices atomically. If true, all devices will be claimed or none will be claimed. Default is true.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» serials|body|[string]|true|A list of serials of devices to claim|
|» detailsByDevice|body|[object]|false|Optional details for claimed devices (currently only used for Catalyst devices)|
|» » serial|body|string|true|The serial of the device these details relate to|

|» » » name|body|string|true|Name of device detail|
|» » » value|body|string|false|Value of device detail|

## Updates the syslog servers configuration for a network.

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkDevicesSyslogServers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/devices/syslog/servers \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "servers": [
      {
        "host": "1.2.3.4",
        "port": 443,
        "roles": [
          "wirelessEventLog",
          "applianceUrlLog"
        ],
        "transportProtocol": "UDP",
        "encryption": {
          "enabled": true,
          "certificate": {
            "id": "1637"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /networks/{networkId}/devices/syslog/servers`

Updates the syslog servers configuration for a network.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "servers": [
    {
      "host": "1.2.3.4",
      "port": 443,
      "roles": [
        "wirelessEventLog",
        "applianceUrlLog"
      ],
      "transportProtocol": "UDP",
      "encryption": {
        "enabled": true,
        "certificate": {
          "id": "1637"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="updates-the-syslog-servers-configuration-for-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» servers|body|[object]|true|A list of the syslog servers for this network; suggested maximum array size is 10|
|» » host|body|string|true|The IP address or FQDN of the syslog server|
|» » port|body|integer|true|The port of the syslog server|
|» » roles|body|[string]|true|A list of roles for the syslog server, specific to Product Type. Options can be found by querying GET api/v1/organizations/:id/devices/syslog/servers/roles/byNetwork and using the value property. Maximum array size is limited by the number of unique roles, which is about 10|
|» » transportProtocol|body|string|false|The transport protocol for the syslog server, defaults to UDP|
|» » encryption|body|object|false|Encryption settings for the syslog server|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|When true, traffic will be encrypted to the syslog server. Defaults to false|
|» » » certificate|body|object|false|The certificate for encryption with the syslog server|
|» » » » id|body|string|false|The ID of the certificate for encryption with the syslog server|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|» » transportProtocol|UDP|

```json
        }
      }

  ]
}
```
