## List the events for the network

<a id="opIdgetNetworkEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/events`

List the events for the network

<h3 id="list-the-events-for-the-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|productType|query|string|false|The product type to fetch events for. This parameter is required for networks with multiple device types. Valid types are wireless, appliance, switch, systemsManager, camera, cellularGateway, wirelessController, campusGateway, and secureConnect|
|includedEventTypes|query|[string]|false|A list of event types. The returned events will be filtered to only include events with these types.|
|excludedEventTypes|query|[string]|false|A list of event types. The returned events will be filtered to exclude events with these types.|
|deviceMac|query|string|false|The MAC address of the Meraki device which the list of events will be filtered with|
|deviceSerial|query|string|false|The serial of the Meraki device which the list of events will be filtered with|
|deviceName|query|string|false|The name of the Meraki device which the list of events will be filtered with|
|clientIp|query|string|false|The IP of the client which the list of events will be filtered with. Only supported for track-by-IP networks.|
|clientMac|query|string|false|The MAC address of the client which the list of events will be filtered with. Only supported for track-by-MAC networks.|
|clientName|query|string|false|The name, or partial name, of the client which the list of events will be filtered with|
|smDeviceMac|query|string|false|The MAC address of the Systems Manager device which the list of events will be filtered with|
|smDeviceName|query|string|false|The name of the Systems Manager device which the list of events will be filtered with|
|eventDetails|query|string|false|The details of the event(Catalyst device only) which the list of events will be filtered with|
|eventSeverity|query|string|false|The severity of the event(Catalyst device only) which the list of events will be filtered with|
|isCatalyst|query|boolean|false|Boolean indicating that whether it is a Catalyst device. For Catalyst device, eventDetails and eventSeverity can be used to filter events.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 10.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|productType|appliance|
|productType|camera|
|productType|campusGateway|
|productType|cellularGateway|
|productType|secureConnect|
|productType|switch|
|productType|systemsManager|
|productType|wireless|
|productType|wirelessController|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Some error",
  "pageStartAt": "2018-02-11T00:00:00.090210Z",
  "pageEndAt": "2018-02-11T00:00:00.090210Z",
  "events": [
    {
      "occurredAt": "2018-02-11T00:00:00.090210Z",
      "networkId": "N_24329156",
      "type": "association",
      "description": "802.11 association",
      "category": "80211",
      "clientId": "k74272e",
      "clientDescription": "Miles's phone",
      "clientMac": "22:33:44:55:66:77",
      "deviceSerial": "Q234-ABCD-5678",
      "deviceName": "My AP",
      "ssidNumber": 1,
      "eventData": {
        "radio": "1",
        "vap": "1",
        "client_mac": "22:33:44:55:66:77",
        "client_ip": "1.2.3.4",
        "channel": "36",
        "rssi": "12",
        "aid": "2104009183"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-the-events-for-the-network-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="list-the-events-for-the-network-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|false|none|A message regarding the events sent. Usually 'null' unless there are no events|
|pageStartAt|string|false|none|An UTC ISO8601 string of the earliest occured at time of the listed events of the page.|
|pageEndAt|string|false|none|An UTC ISO8601 string of the latest occured at time of the listed events of the page.|
|events|[object]|false|none|An array of events that took place in the network.|
|» occurredAt|string|false|none|An UTC ISO8601 string of the time the event occurred at.|
|» networkId|string|false|none|The ID of the network.|
|» type|string|false|none|The type of event being listed.|
|» description|string|false|none|A description of the event the happened.|
|» category|string|false|none|The category that the event type belongs to|
|» clientId|string|false|none|A string identifying the client. This could be a client's MAC or IP address|
|» clientDescription|string|false|none|A description of the client. This is usually the client's device name.|
|» clientMac|string|false|none|The client's MAC address.|
|» deviceSerial|string|false|none|The serial number of the device. Only shown if the device is an access point.|
|» deviceName|string|false|none|The name of the device. Only shown if the device is an access point.|
|» ssidNumber|integer|false|none|The SSID number of the device.|
|» eventData|object|false|none|An object containing more data related to the event.|
|» » radio|string|false|none|The radio band number the client is trying to connect to.|
|» » vap|string|false|none|The virtual access point (VAP) number the client is connecting to.|
|» » client_mac|string|false|none|The client's MAC address|
|» » client_ip|string|false|none|The client's IP address|
|» » channel|string|false|none|The radio channel the client is connecting to.|
|» » rssi|string|false|none|The current received signal strength indication (RSSI) of the client connected to an AP.|
|» » aid|string|false|none|The association ID of the client.|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Link|string||A comma-separated list of first, last, prev, and next relative links used for subsequent paginated requests.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: dashboard:general:telemetry:read )
</aside>

## Update firmware upgrade information for a network

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkFirmwareUpgrades"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/firmwareUpgrades \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "upgradeWindow": {
      "dayOfWeek": "sun",
      "hourOfDay": "4:00"
    },
    "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
    "products": {

        "nextUpgrade": {

          "toVersion": {
            "id": "1000"
          }
        },
        "participateInNextBetaRelease": false
      },

          }
        },
        "participateInNextBetaRelease": false
      },
      "switch": {

          }
        },
        "participateInNextBetaRelease": false
      },
      "camera": {
        "nextUpgrade": {
          "time": "2019-03-17T17:22:52Z",
          "toVersion": {
            "id": "1003"
          }
        },
        "participateInNextBetaRelease": false
      },
      "cellularGateway": {
        "nextUpgrade": {
          "time": "2019-03-17T17:22:52Z",
          "toVersion": {
            "id": "1004"
          }
        },
        "participateInNextBetaRelease": false
      },
      "sensor": {
        "nextUpgrade": {
          "time": "2019-03-17T17:22:52Z",
          "toVersion": {
            "id": "1005"
          }
        },
        "participateInNextBetaRelease": false
      },
      "wirelessController": {
        "nextUpgrade": {
          "time": "2019-03-17T17:22:52Z",
          "toVersion": {
            "id": "1006"
          }
        },
        "participateInNextBetaRelease": false
      },
      "campusGateway": {
        "nextUpgrade": {
          "strategy": "minimizeUpgradeTime",
          "time": "2019-03-17T17:22:52Z",
          "toVersion": {

        },
```

## Rollback a Firmware Upgrade For A Network

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkFirmwareUpgradesRollback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/firmwareUpgrades/rollbacks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "product": "switch",
    "time": "2020-10-21T02:00:00Z",
    "reasons": [
      {
        "category": "performance",
        "comment": "Network was slower with the upgrade"
      }
    ],
    "toVersion": {
      "id": "7857"
    },
    "predownload": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/firmwareUpgrades/rollbacks`

Rollback a Firmware Upgrade For A Network

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "product": "switch",
  "time": "2020-10-21T02:00:00Z",
  "reasons": [
    {
      "category": "performance",
      "comment": "Network was slower with the upgrade"
    }
  ],
  "toVersion": {
    "id": "7857"
  },
  "predownload": {
    "enabled": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="rollback-a-firmware-upgrade-for-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» product|body|string|false|Product type to rollback (if the network is a combined network)|
|» time|body|string(date-time)|false|Scheduled time for the rollback|
|» reasons|body|[object]|true|Reasons for the rollback|
|» » category|body|string|true|Reason for the rollback|
|» » comment|body|string|true|Additional comment about the rollback|
|» toVersion|body|object|false|Version to downgrade to (if the network has firmware flexibility)|
|» » id|body|string|false|The version ID|
|» predownload|body|object|false|Predownload settings for the firmware upgrade|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether or not the network devices will predownload the firmware image in advance of the actual upgrade. Only applies to wireless devices running MR 32 or higher.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» product|appliance|
|» product|camera|
|» product|campusGateway|
|» product|cellularGateway|
|» product|secureConnect|
|» product|switch|
|» product|switchCatalyst|
|» product|wireless|
|» product|wirelessController|
|» » category|broke old features|
|» » category|other|
|» » category|performance|
|» » category|stability|
|» » category|testing|
|» » category|unifying networks versions|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "product": "switch",
  "status": "pending",
  "upgradeBatchId": "23456",
  "time": "2020-10-21T02:00:00Z",
  "toVersion": {
    "id": "7857",
    "firmware": "switch-15-5-2",
    "shortName": "MS 25.5.2",
    "releaseType": "stable",
    "releaseDate": "2020-03-28T17:22:52Z"
  },
  "reasons": [
    {
      "category": "performance",
      "comment": "Network was slower with the upgrade"
    }
  ],
  "predownload": {
    "enabled": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="rollback-a-firmware-upgrade-for-a-network-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

## Schedule auto locate jobs for one or more floor plans in a network

<a id="opIdbatchNetworkFloorPlansAutoLocateJobs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/floorPlans/autoLocate/jobs/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "jobs": [
      {
        "floorPlanId": "g_2176982374",
        "refresh": [
          "gnss",
          "ranging"
        ],
        "scheduledAt": "2018-02-11T00:00:00Z"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/floorPlans/autoLocate/jobs/batch`

Schedule auto locate jobs for one or more floor plans in a network

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "jobs": [
    {
      "floorPlanId": "g_2176982374",
      "refresh": [
        "gnss",
        "ranging"
      ],
      "scheduledAt": "2018-02-11T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="schedule-auto-locate-jobs-for-one-or-more-floor-plans-in-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» jobs|body|[object]|true|The list of auto locate jobs to be scheduled. Up to 100 jobs can be provided in a request.|
|» » floorPlanId|body|string|true|The ID of the floor plan to run auto locate for|
|» » refresh|body|[string]|false|The types of location data that should be refreshed for this job. The list must either contain both 'gnss' and 'ranging' or be empty, as we currently only support refreshing both 'gnss' and 'ranging', or neither.|
|» » scheduledAt|body|string(date-time)|false|Timestamp in ISO8601 format which indicates when the auto locate job should be run. If omitted, the auto locate job will start immediately.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "jobs": [
    {
      "id": "1234",
      "networkId": "N_24329156",
      "floorPlanId": "g_2176982374",
      "status": "error",
      "scheduledAt": "2018-02-11T00:00:00Z",
      "completed": {
        "percentage": 50
      },
      "ranging": {
        "status": "in progress",
        "completed": {
          "percentage": 24
        }
      },
      "gnss": {
        "status": "in progress",
        "completed": {
          "percentage": 4
        }
      },
      "errors": [
        {
          "source": "ranging",
          "type": "missing anchors"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|jobs|[object]|false|none|The newly created jobs|

|» networkId|string|false|none|Network ID|
|» floorPlanId|string|false|none|Floor plan ID|

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/floorPlans/string \
```

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of your floor plan.|
|» center|body|object|false|The longitude and latitude of the center of your floor plan. If you want to change the geolocation data of your floor plan, either the 'center' or two adjacent corners (e.g. 'topLeftCorner' and 'bottomLeftCorner') must be specified. If 'center' is specified, the floor plan is placed over that point with no rotation. If two adjacent corners are specified, the floor plan is rotated to line up with the two specified points. The aspect ratio of the floor plan's image is preserved regardless of which corners/center are specified. (This means if that more than two corners are specified, only two corners may be used to preserve the floor plan's aspect ratio.). No two points can have the same latitude, longitude pair.|
|» » lat|body|number(float)|true|Latitude|
|» » lng|body|number(float)|true|Longitude|
|» bottomLeftCorner|body|object|false|The longitude and latitude of the bottom left corner of your floor plan.|

|» » lng|body|number(float)|true|Longitude|
|» floorNumber|body|number(float)|false|The floor number of the floors within the building|
|» imageContents|body|string(byte)|false|The file contents (a base 64 encoded string) of your new image. Supported formats are PNG, GIF, and JPG. Note that all images are saved as PNG files, regardless of the format they are uploaded in. If you upload a new image, and you do NOT specify any new geolocation fields ('center, 'topLeftCorner', etc), the floor plan will be recentered with no rotation in order to maintain the aspect ratio of your new image.|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/groupPolicies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "No video streaming",
    "scheduling": {
      "enabled": true,
      "monday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "tuesday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "wednesday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "thursday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "friday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "saturday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "sunday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      }
    },
    "bandwidth": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "bandwidthLimits": {
        "limitUp": 1000000,
        "limitDown": 1000000
      }
    },
    "firewallAndTrafficShaping": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "trafficShapingRules": [
        {
          "definitions": [
            {
              "type": "host",
              "value": "google.com"
            }
          ],
          "perClientBandwidthLimits": {
            "settings": "custom",
            "bandwidthLimits": {
              "limitUp": 1000000,
              "limitDown": 1000000
            }
          },
          "dscpTagValue": 0,
          "pcpTagValue": 0,
          "priority": "normal"
        }
      ],
      "l3FirewallRules": [
        {
          "comment": "Allow TCP traffic to subnet with HTTP servers.",
          "policy": "allow",
          "protocol": "tcp",
          "destPort": "443",
          "destCidr": "192.168.1.0/24"
        }
      ],
      "l7FirewallRules": [
        {
          "policy": "deny",
          "type": "host",
          "value": "google.com"
        }
      ]
    },
    "contentFiltering": {
      "allowedUrlPatterns": {
        "settings": "network default",
        "patterns": []
      },
      "blockedUrlPatterns": {
        "settings": "append",
        "patterns": [
          "http://www.example.com",
          "http://www.betting.com"
        ]
      },
      "blockedUrlCategories": {
        "settings": "override",
        "categories": [
          "meraki:contentFiltering/category/1",
          "meraki:contentFiltering/category/7"
        ]
      }
    },
    "splashAuthSettings": "bypass",
    "vlanTagging": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "vlanId": "1"
    },
    "bonjourForwarding": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "rules": [
        {
          "description": "A simple bonjour rule",
          "vlanId": "1",
          "services": [
            "All Services"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

## Update a group policy

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkGroupPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/groupPolicies/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "No video streaming",
    "scheduling": {
      "enabled": true,
      "monday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "tuesday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "wednesday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "thursday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "friday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "saturday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      },
      "sunday": {
        "active": true,
        "from": "9:00",
        "to": "17:00"
      }
    },
    "bandwidth": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "bandwidthLimits": {
        "limitUp": 1000000,
        "limitDown": 1000000
      }
    },
    "firewallAndTrafficShaping": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "trafficShapingRules": [
        {
          "definitions": [
            {
              "type": "host",
              "value": "google.com"
            }
          ],
          "perClientBandwidthLimits": {
            "settings": "custom",
            "bandwidthLimits": {
              "limitUp": 1000000,
              "limitDown": 1000000
            }
          },
          "dscpTagValue": 0,
          "pcpTagValue": 0,
          "priority": "normal"
        }
      ],
      "l3FirewallRules": [
        {
          "comment": "Allow TCP traffic to subnet with HTTP servers.",
          "policy": "allow",
          "protocol": "tcp",
          "destPort": "443",
          "destCidr": "192.168.1.0/24"
        }
      ],
      "l7FirewallRules": [
        {
          "policy": "deny",
          "type": "host",
          "value": "google.com"
        }
      ]
    },
    "contentFiltering": {
      "allowedUrlPatterns": {
        "settings": "network default",
        "patterns": []
      },
      "blockedUrlPatterns": {
        "settings": "append",
        "patterns": [
          "http://www.example.com",
          "http://www.betting.com"
        ]
      },
      "blockedUrlCategories": {
        "settings": "override",
        "categories": [
          "meraki:contentFiltering/category/1",
          "meraki:contentFiltering/category/7"
        ]
      }
    },
    "splashAuthSettings": "bypass",
    "vlanTagging": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "vlanId": "1"
    },
    "bonjourForwarding": {
      "settings": "custom",
      "rules": [
        {
          "description": "A simple bonjour rule",
          "vlanId": "1",
          "services": [
            "All Services"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

## Authorize a user configured with Meraki Authentication for a network (currently supports 802.1X, splash guest, and client VPN users, and currently, organizations have a 50,000 user cap)

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkMerakiAuthUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/merakiAuthUsers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "miles@meraki.com",
    "name": "Miles Meraki",
    "password": "secret",
    "accountType": "802.1X",
    "emailPasswordToUser": false,
    "isAdmin": false,
    "authorizations": [
      {
        "ssidNumber": 1,
        "expiresAt": "2018-03-13T00:00:00.090210Z"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/merakiAuthUsers`

Authorize a user configured with Meraki Authentication for a network (currently supports 802.1X, splash guest, and client VPN users, and currently, organizations have a 50,000 user cap)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "miles@meraki.com",
  "name": "Miles Meraki",
  "password": "secret",
  "accountType": "802.1X",
  "emailPasswordToUser": false,
  "isAdmin": false,
  "authorizations": [
    {
      "ssidNumber": 1,
      "expiresAt": "2018-03-13T00:00:00.090210Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="authorize-a-user-configured-with-meraki-authentication-for-a-network-currently-supports-8021x-splash-guest-and-client-vpn-users-and-currently-organizations-have-a-50000-user-cap-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» email|body|string|true|Email address of the user|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the user. Only required If the user is not a Dashboard administrator.|
|» password|body|string|false|The password for this user account. Only required If the user is not a Dashboard administrator.|
|» accountType|body|string|false|Authorization type for user. Can be 'Guest' or '802.1X' for wireless networks, or 'Client VPN' for MX networks. Defaults to '802.1X'.|
|» emailPasswordToUser|body|boolean|false|Whether or not Meraki should email the password to user. Default is false.|
|» isAdmin|body|boolean|false|Whether or not the user is a Dashboard administrator.|
|» authorizations|body|[object]|true|Authorization zones and expiration dates for the user.|
|» » ssidNumber|body|integer|false|Required for wireless networks. The SSID for which the user is being authorized, which must be configured for the user's given accountType.|
|» » expiresAt|body|string|false|Date for authorization to expire. Set to 'Never' for the authorization to not expire, which is the default.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» accountType|802.1X|
|» accountType|Client VPN|
|» accountType|Guest|

```json
    }
  ]
}
```

Submit a new delete or restrict processing PII request


```json
{
  "type": "delete",
  "datasets": [
    "usage",
    "events"
  ],
  "username": "milesmeraki",
  "email": "miles@meraki.com",
  "mac": "00:11:22:33:44:55",

}
```

<h3 id="submit-a-new-delete-or-restrict-processing-pii-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|false|One of "delete" or "restrict processing"|
|» datasets|body|[string]|false|The datasets related to the provided key that should be deleted. Only applies to "delete" requests. The value "all" will be expanded to all datasets applicable to this type. The datasets by applicable to each type are: mac (usage, events, traffic), email (users, loginAttempts), username (users, loginAttempts), bluetoothMac (client, connectivity), smDeviceId (device), smUserId (user)|
|» username|body|string|false|The username of a network log in. Only applies to "delete" requests.|
|» email|body|string|false|The email of a network user account. Only applies to "delete" requests.|
|» mac|body|string|false|The MAC of a network client device. Applies to both "restrict processing" and "delete" requests.|
|» smDeviceId|body|string|false|The sm_device_id of a Systems Manager device. The only way to "restrict processing" or "delete" a Systems Manager device. Must include "device" in the dataset for a "delete" request to destroy the device.|
|» smUserId|body|string|false|The sm_user_id of a Systems Manager user. The only way to "restrict processing" or "delete" a Systems Manager user. Must include "user" in the dataset for a "delete" request to destroy the user.|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/snmp \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/snmp`

Return the SNMP settings for a network

<h3 id="return-the-snmp-settings-for-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access": "users",
  "communityString": "sample",
  "users": [
    {
      "username": "AzureDiamond",
      "passphrase": "hunter2"
    }
  ],
  "authentication": {
    "protocol": "SHA-1"
  },
  "privacy": {
    "protocol": "AES-128"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="return-the-snmp-settings-for-a-network-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-the-snmp-settings-for-a-network-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access|string|false|none|The type of SNMP access. Can be one of 'none' (disabled), 'community' (V1/V2c), or 'users' (V3).|
|communityString|string|false|none|SNMP community string if access is 'community'.|
|users|[object]|false|none|SNMP settings if access is 'users'.|
|» username|string|false|none|The username for the SNMP user.|
|» passphrase|string|false|none|The passphrase for the SNMP user.|
|authentication|object|false|none|SNMPv3 authentication settings. Applicable only if 'access' is 'users'.|
|» protocol|string|false|none|The SNMPv3 authentication protocol.|
|privacy|object|false|none|SNMPv3 privacy settings. Applicable only if 'access' is 'users'.|
|» protocol|string|false|none|The SNMPv3 privacy protocol.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» protocol|SHA-1|
|» protocol|SHA-256|
|» protocol|SHA-384|
|» protocol|SHA-512|
|» protocol|AES-128|
|» protocol|DES|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: dashboard:general:telemetry:read )
</aside>

## Update the SNMP settings for a network

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkSnmp"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/snmp \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "access": "users",
    "communityString": "sample",
    "users": [
      {
        "username": "AzureDiamond",
        "passphrase": "hunter2"
      }
    ],
    "authentication": {
      "protocol": "SHA-1"
    },
    "privacy": {
      "protocol": "AES-128"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /networks/{networkId}/snmp`

Update the SNMP settings for a network

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access": "users",
  "communityString": "sample",
  "users": [
    {
      "username": "AzureDiamond",
      "passphrase": "hunter2"
    }
  ],
  "authentication": {
    "protocol": "SHA-1"
  },
  "privacy": {
    "protocol": "AES-128"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-snmp-settings-for-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» access|body|string|false|The type of SNMP access. Can be one of 'none' (disabled), 'community' (V1/V2c), or 'users' (V3).|
|» communityString|body|string|false|The SNMP community string. Only relevant if 'access' is set to 'community'.|
|» users|body|[object]|false|The list of SNMP users. Only relevant if 'access' is set to 'users'.|
|» » username|body|string|true|The username for the SNMP user. Required.|
|» » passphrase|body|string|true|The passphrase for the SNMP user. Required.|
|» authentication|body|object|false|SNMPv3 authentication settings. Only relevant if 'access' is set to 'users'.|
|» » protocol|body|string|false|The SNMPv3 authentication protocol.|
|» privacy|body|object|false|SNMPv3 privacy settings. Only relevant if 'access' is set to 'users'.|
|» » protocol|body|string|false|The SNMPv3 privacy protocol.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» access|community|
|» access|none|
|» access|users|
|» » protocol|SHA-1|
|» » protocol|SHA-256|
|» » protocol|SHA-384|
|» » protocol|SHA-512|
|» » protocol|AES-128|
|» » protocol|DES|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access": "users",
  "communityString": "sample",
  "users": [
    {
      "username": "AzureDiamond",
      "passphrase": "hunter2"
    }
  ],
  "authentication": {
    "protocol": "SHA-1"
  },
  "privacy": {
    "protocol": "AES-128"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-snmp-settings-for-a-network-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="update-the-snmp-settings-for-a-network-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access|string|false|none|The type of SNMP access. Can be one of 'none' (disabled), 'community' (V1/V2c), or 'users' (V3).|
|communityString|string|false|none|SNMP community string if access is 'community'.|
|users|[object]|false|none|SNMP settings if access is 'users'.|
|» username|string|false|none|The username for the SNMP user.|
|» passphrase|string|false|none|The passphrase for the SNMP user.|
|authentication|object|false|none|SNMPv3 authentication settings. Applicable only if 'access' is 'users'.|
|» protocol|string|false|none|The SNMPv3 authentication protocol.|
|privacy|object|false|none|SNMPv3 privacy settings. Applicable only if 'access' is 'users'.|
|» protocol|string|false|none|The SNMPv3 privacy protocol.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» protocol|SHA-1|
|» protocol|SHA-256|

## Return the traffic analysis data for this network

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 30 days from today.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameter t0. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 30 days.|
|deviceType|query|string|false|Filter the data by device type: 'combined', 'wireless', 'switch' or 'appliance'. Defaults to 'combined'. When using 'combined', for each rule the data will come from the device type with the most usage.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|deviceType|appliance|
|deviceType|combined|
|deviceType|switch|
|deviceType|wireless|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "application": "Gmail",
    "destination": "2.3.4.5",
    "protocol": "TCP",
    "port": 443,
    "sent": 138,
    "recv": 61,
    "numClients": 7,
    "activeTime": 77000,
    "flows": 300
  }
]
```

## List the clients of a device, up to a maximum of a month ago

<a id="opIdgetDeviceClients"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/clients \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /devices/{serial}/clients`

List the clients of a device, up to a maximum of a month ago. The usage of each client is returned in kilobytes. If the device is a switch, the switchport is returned; otherwise the switchport field is null. Wireless connection metadata reflects the latest available successful association event in the selected period.

<h3 id="list-the-clients-of-a-device-up-to-a-maximum-of-a-month-ago-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameter t0. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "k74272e",
    "mac": "22:33:44:55:66:77",
    "description": "Miles's phone",
    "mdnsName": "Miles's phone",
    "dhcpHostname": "MilesPhone",
    "user": "milesmeraki",
    "ip": "1.2.3.4",
    "vlan": "100",
    "namedVlan": "My VLAN",
    "switchport": "My switch port",
    "adaptivePolicyGroup": "101",
    "usage": {
      "sent": 138,
      "recv": 61
    }
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-the-clients-of-a-device-up-to-a-maximum-of-a-month-ago-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="list-the-clients-of-a-device-up-to-a-maximum-of-a-month-ago-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|false|none|The ID of the client|
|» mac|string|false|none|The MAC address of the client|
|» description|string|false|none|Short description of the client|
|» mdnsName|string|false|none|The client's MDNS name|
|» dhcpHostname|string|false|none|The client's DHCP hostname|
|» user|string|false|none|The client user's name|
|» ip|string|false|none|The IP address of the client|
|» vlan|string|false|none|The client-assigned name of the VLAN the client is connected to|
|» namedVlan|string|false|none|The owner-assigned name of the VLAN the client is connected to|
|» switchport|string|false|none|The name of the switchport with clients on it, if the device is a switch|
|» adaptivePolicyGroup|string|false|none|A description of the adaptive policy group|
|» usage|object|false|none|Client usage data for sent and received|
|» » sent|number(float)|false|none|Usage sent by the client|
|» » recv|number(float)|false|none|Usage received by the client|

## Enqueue a job to perform a ARP table request for the device

<a id="opIdcreateDeviceLiveToolsArpTable"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/liveTools/arpTable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "callback": {
      "url": "https://webhook.site/28efa24e-f830-4d9f-a12b-fbb9e5035031",
      "sharedSecret": "secret",
      "httpServer": {
        "id": "aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZXhhbXBsZS5jb20vd2ViaG9va3M="
      },
      "payloadTemplate": {
        "id": "wpt_2100"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /devices/{serial}/liveTools/arpTable`

Enqueue a job to perform a ARP table request for the device. This endpoint currently supports switches, wireless access points, and catalyst routers. This endpoint has a sustained rate limit of one request every five seconds per device, with an allowed burst of five requests.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "callback": {
    "url": "https://webhook.site/28efa24e-f830-4d9f-a12b-fbb9e5035031",
    "sharedSecret": "secret",
    "httpServer": {
      "id": "aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZXhhbXBsZS5jb20vd2ViaG9va3M="
    },
    "payloadTemplate": {
      "id": "wpt_2100"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="enqueue-a-job-to-perform-a-arp-table-request-for-the-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» callback|body|object|false|Details for the callback. Please include either an httpServerId OR url and sharedSecret|
|» » url|body|string|false|The callback URL for the webhook target. If using this field, please also specify a sharedSecret.|
|» » sharedSecret|body|string|false|A shared secret that will be included in the requests sent to the callback URL. It can be used to verify that the request was sent by Meraki. If using this field, please also specify an url.|
|» » httpServer|body|object|false|The webhook receiver used for the callback webhook.|
|» » » id|body|string|false|The webhook receiver ID that will receive information. If specifying this, please leave the url and sharedSecret fields blank.|
|» » payloadTemplate|body|object|false|The payload template of the webhook used for the callback|
|» » » id|body|string|false|The ID of the payload template. Defaults to 'wpt_00005' for the Callback (included) template.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "arpTableId": "1284392014819",
  "url": "/devices/Q234-ABCD-5678/liveTools/arpTable/1284392014819",
  "request": {
    "serial": "Q234-ABCD-5678"
  },
  "status": "complete",
  "callback": {
    "id": "1284392014819",
    "url": "https://webhook.site/28efa24e-f830-4d9f-a12b-fbb9e5035031",
    "status": "new"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="enqueue-a-job-to-perform-a-arp-table-request-for-the-device-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="enqueue-a-job-to-perform-a-arp-table-request-for-the-device-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|arpTableId|string|false|none|Id of the ARP table request. Used to check the status of the request.|
|url|string|false|none|GET this url to check the status of your ARP table request.|
|request|object|false|none|ARP table request parameters|
|» serial|string|false|none|Device serial number|
|status|string|false|none|Status of the ARP table request.|
|callback|object|false|none|Information for callback used to send back results|
|» id|string|false|none|The ID of the callback. To check the status of the callback, use this ID in a request to /webhooks/callbacks/statuses/{id}|
|» url|string|false|none|The callback URL for the webhook target. This was either provided in the original request or comes from a configured webhook receiver|
|» status|string|false|none|The status of the callback|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|

|status|failed|
|status|new|
|status|ready|

|status|scheduled|

`POST /devices/{serial}/liveTools/macTable`

`POST /devices/{serial}/liveTools/pingDevice`

```json
  "count": 3,
```

`POST /devices/{serial}/liveTools/power/usage`

Enqueues a live tool job that retrieves details about a device's overall power usage. This endpoint has a sustained rate limit of one request every five seconds per device, with an allowed burst of five requests.

`POST /devices/{serial}/liveTools/routingTable/lookups`

```json
    },
    "payloadTemplate": {

    }
  }
}
```

`POST /devices/{serial}/liveTools/wakeOnLan`

Enqueue a job to send a Wake-on-LAN packet from the device. This endpoint has a sustained rate limit of one request every five seconds per device, with an allowed burst of five requests.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "vlanId": 12,
  "mac": "00:11:22:33:44:55",
  "callback": {
    "url": "https://webhook.site/28efa24e-f830-4d9f-a12b-fbb9e5035031",
    "sharedSecret": "secret",
    "httpServer": {
      "id": "aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZXhhbXBsZS5jb20vd2ViaG9va3M="
    },
    "payloadTemplate": {
      "id": "wpt_2100"
    }
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» vlanId|body|integer|true|The target's VLAN (1 to 4094)|
|» mac|body|string|true|The target's MAC address|
|» callback|body|object|false|Details for the callback. Please include either an httpServerId OR url and sharedSecret|
|» » url|body|string|false|The callback URL for the webhook target. If using this field, please also specify a sharedSecret.|
|» » sharedSecret|body|string|false|A shared secret that will be included in the requests sent to the callback URL. It can be used to verify that the request was sent by Meraki. If using this field, please also specify an url.|
|» » httpServer|body|object|false|The webhook receiver used for the callback webhook.|
|» » » id|body|string|false|The webhook receiver ID that will receive information. If specifying this, please leave the url and sharedSecret fields blank.|
|» » payloadTemplate|body|object|false|The payload template of the webhook used for the callback|
|» » » id|body|string|false|The ID of the payload template. Defaults to 'wpt_00005' for the Callback (included) template.|

<a id="opIdupdateDeviceWirelessRadioOverrides"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/wireless/radio/overrides \

  -d '{

    },
    "radios": [

        "channel": 149,
        "targetPower": 15,
        "channelWidth": 20
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /devices/{serial}/wireless/radio/overrides`

Update 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz radio settings (channel, channel width, power, and enable/disable) that override RF profiles. Read-only fields returned by this endpoint, such as 'serial', 'network', and 'radios[].band', may be included when sending a previously returned object back to this PUT endpoint and will be ignored.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "rfProfile": {
    "id": "1234"
  },
  "radios": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "index": "1",
      "channel": 149,
      "targetPower": 15,
      "channelWidth": 20
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-24-ghz-5-ghz-and-6-ghz-radio-settings-channel-channel-width-power-and-enabledisable-that-override-rf-profiles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» rfProfile|body|object|false|This device's RF profile. If omitted, the existing RF profile assignment remains unchanged.|
|» » id|body|string \| null|false|The ID of an RF profile to assign to the device. If this field is omitted, the device's existing RF profile assignment will remain unchanged. If the value of this parameter is null, the appropriate basic RF profile (indoor or outdoor) will be assigned to the device. Assigning an RF profile will clear ALL manually configured overrides on the device (channel width, channel, power).|
|» radios|body|[object]|false|Radio overrides. If omitted, existing per-radio override settings remain unchanged. If provided, only the radios included in the array are updated; the array does not replace the device's full existing set of radio overrides. Read-only response fields for each radio, such as 'band', may be included in the request body and are ignored.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable radio. Setting to false will set tx power to -1.|
|» » index|body|string|true|Indicates which radio to override|
|» » channel|body|integer \| null|false|Sets a radio override channel. Can be null to use auto channel.|
|» » targetPower|body|integer \| null|false|Set a radio override target power (dBm). Can be null to use auto power range.|
|» » channelWidth|body|integer \| null|false|Set a radio override channel width. Can be null to use auto channel width.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "serial": "Q234-ABCD-5678",
  "network": {
    "id": "N_24329156"
  },
  "rfProfile": {
    "id": "1234"
  },
  "radios": [
    {
      "enabled": true,
      "index": "1",
      "band": "5",
      "channel": 149,
      "channelWidth": 20,
      "targetPower": 15
    }
  ]
}
```

## Creates a new rule

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkWirelessAirMarshalRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/wireless/airMarshal/rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "allow",
    "match": {
      "type": "bssid",
      "string": "00:11:22:33:44:55"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/wireless/airMarshal/rules`

Creates a new rule. In an action batch, mutations execute in the submitted order and commit atomically; a failure rolls back every mutation and configuration update in that batch. Completed or failed batches cannot be executed again. Air Marshal settings updates may be included in the same batch. The created rule ID is returned in the action batch createdResources list. A later action in the same batch cannot reference that generated ID.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "allow",
  "match": {
    "type": "bssid",
    "string": "00:11:22:33:44:55"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-new-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|Indicates if this rule will allow, block, or alert.|
|» match|body|object|true|Object describing the rule specification.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of match.|
|» » string|body|string|true|The string used to match.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|alert|
|» type|allow|
|» type|block|
|» » type|bssid|
|» » type|contains|
|» » type|exact|
|» » type|wildcard|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "network": {
    "id": "N_12345",
    "name": "Network 1"
  },
  "ruleId": "5239",
  "type": "allow",
  "updatedAt": "2023-05-23 12:02:46.298",
  "createdAt": "2023-05-23 12:02:46.298",
  "match": {
    "string": "ipsum",
    "type": "contains"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-new-rule-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="creates-a-new-rule-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

## Return the latency history for a client

<a id="opIdgetNetworkWirelessClientLatencyHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/wireless/clients/string/latencyHistory \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/wireless/clients/{clientId}/latencyHistory`

Return the latency history for a client. Clients can be identified by a client key or either the MAC or IP depending on whether the network uses Track-by-IP. The latency data is from a sample of 2% of packets and is grouped into 4 traffic categories: background, best effort, video, voice. Within these categories the sampled packet counters are bucketed by latency in milliseconds.

<h3 id="return-the-latency-history-for-a-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|clientId|path|string|true|Client ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 791 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 791 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 791 days. The default is 1 day.|
|resolution|query|integer|false|The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 86400. The default is 86400.|

> 200 Response

```json

  {
    "t0": 1550534400,
    "t1": 1550620800,
    "latencyBinsByCategory": {
      "backgroundTraffic": {
        "0.5": 41750,
        "1.0": 21552,
        "2.0": 59940,
        "4.0": 146622,
        "8.0": 57354,
        "16.0": 0,

        "128.0": 0,

      },

        "0.5": 1840899,
        "1.0": 1644506,
```

## Aggregated latency info for a given client on this network

<a id="opIdgetNetworkWirelessClientLatencyStats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/wireless/clients/string/latencyStats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/wireless/clients/{clientId}/latencyStats`

Aggregated latency info for a given client on this network. Clients are identified by their MAC.

<h3 id="aggregated-latency-info-for-a-given-client-on-this-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|clientId|path|string|true|Client ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 180 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 7 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 7 days.|
|band|query|string|false|Filter results by band (either '2.4', '5' or '6'). Note that data prior to February 2020 will not have band information.|
|ssid|query|integer|false|Filter results by SSID|
|apTag|query|string|false|Filter results by AP Tag|
|vlan|query|integer|false|Filter results by VLAN|
|fields|query|string|false|Partial selection: If present, this call will return only the selected fields of ["rawDistribution", "avg"]. All fields will be returned by default. Selected fields must be entered as a comma separated string.|

|Parameter|Value|

|band|5|

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/wireless/dataRateHistory \
```

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/wireless/dataRateHistory`

Return PHY data rates over time for a network, device, or network client

<h3 id="return-phy-data-rates-over-time-for-a-network-device-or-network-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 7 days.|
|resolution|query|integer|false|The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 300, 600, 1200, 3600, 14400, 86400. The default is 86400.|
|autoResolution|query|boolean|false|Automatically select a data resolution based on the given timespan; this overrides the value specified by the 'resolution' parameter. The default setting is false.|
|clientId|query|string|false|Filter results by network client.|
|deviceSerial|query|string|false|Filter results by device.|
|apTag|query|string|false|Filter results by AP tag.|
|band|query|string|false|Filter results by band (either '2.4', '5' or '6').|
|ssid|query|integer|false|Filter results by SSID number.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|band|2.4|
|band|5|
|band|6|

## Return average wireless latency over time for a network, device, or network client

<a id="opIdgetNetworkWirelessLatencyHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/wireless/latencyHistory \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/wireless/latencyHistory`

Return average wireless latency over time for a network, device, or network client

<h3 id="return-average-wireless-latency-over-time-for-a-network-device-or-network-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 7 days.|
|resolution|query|integer|false|The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 300, 600, 1200, 3600, 14400, 86400. The default is 86400.|
|autoResolution|query|boolean|false|Automatically select a data resolution based on the given timespan; this overrides the value specified by the 'resolution' parameter. The default setting is false.|
|clientId|query|string|false|Filter results by network client.|
|deviceSerial|query|string|false|Filter results by device.|
|apTag|query|string|false|Filter results by AP tag.|
|band|query|string|false|Filter results by band (either '2.4', '5' or '6').|
|ssid|query|integer|false|Filter results by SSID number.|
|accessCategory|query|string|false|Filter by access category.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|band|2.4|
|band|5|
|band|6|
|accessCategory|backgroundTraffic|
|accessCategory|bestEffortTraffic|
|accessCategory|videoTraffic|
|accessCategory|voiceTraffic|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "startTs": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "endTs": "2020-01-01T01:00:00Z",
    "avgLatencyMs": 29
  }
]
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-average-wireless-latency-over-time-for-a-network-device-or-network-client-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» startTs|string(date-time)|false|none|The start time of the query range|
|» endTs|string(date-time)|false|none|The end time of the query range|
|» avgLatencyMs|integer|false|none|Average latency in milliseconds|

## Creates new RF profile for this network

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/wireless/rfProfiles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Main Office",
    "clientBalancingEnabled": true,
    "minBitrateType": "band",
    "bandSelectionType": "ap",
    "apBandSettings": {
      "bandOperationMode": "dual",
      "bands": {
        "enabled": [
          "2.4",
          "5"
        ]
      },
      "bandSteeringEnabled": true

      "minPower": 5,

        6,
        11
      ],
      "axEnabled": true,
      "dot11ax": {
        "enabled": true
      },
      "rxsop": -95
    },
    "fiveGhzSettings": {
      "maxPower": 30,
      "minPower": 8,
      "minBitrate": 12,
      "validAutoChannels": [
        36,
        40,
        44,
        48,
        52,
        56,
        60,
        64,
        100,
        104,
        108,
        112,
        116,
        120,
        124,
        128,
        132,
        136,
        140,
        144,
        149,
        153,
        157,
        161,
        165
      ],
      "channelWidth": "auto",
      "dot11ax": {
        "enabled": true
      },
      "rxsop": -95
    },
    "sixGhzSettings": {
      "maxPower": 30,
      "minPower": 8,
      "minBitrate": 12,
      "validAutoChannels": [
```

<h3 id="creates-new-rf-profile-for-this-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new profile. Must be unique. This param is required on creation.|
|» clientBalancingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Steers client to best available access point. Can be either true or false. Defaults to true.|
|» minBitrateType|body|string|false|Minimum bitrate can be set to either 'band' or 'ssid'. Defaults to band.|
|» bandSelectionType|body|string|true|Band selection can be set to either 'ssid' or 'ap'. This param is required on creation.|
|» apBandSettings|body|object|false|Settings that will be enabled if selectionType is set to 'ap'.|
|» » bandOperationMode|body|string|false|Choice between 'dual', '2.4ghz', '5ghz', '6ghz' or 'multi'. Defaults to dual.|
|» » bands|body|object|false|Settings related to all bands|
|» » » enabled|body|[string]|false|List of enabled bands. Can include ["2.4", "5", "6", "disabled"]|
|» » bandSteeringEnabled|body|boolean|false|Steers client to most open band. Can be either true or false. Defaults to true.|
|» twoFourGhzSettings|body|object|false|Settings related to 2.4Ghz band|
|» » maxPower|body|integer|false|Sets max power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» » minPower|body|integer|false|Sets min power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 5.|
|» » minBitrate|body|number(float)|false|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '2', '5.5', '6', '9', '11', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 11.|
|» » validAutoChannels|body|[integer]|false|Sets valid auto channels for 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '6' or '11'. Defaults to [1, 6, 11].|
|» » axEnabled|body|boolean|false|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Deprecated; use dot11ax.enabled instead. Defaults to true.|
|» » dot11ax|body|object|false|IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) settings.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Defaults to true.|
|» » rxsop|body|integer \| null|false|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|
|» fiveGhzSettings|body|object|false|Settings related to 5Ghz band|
|» » maxPower|body|integer|false|Sets max power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» » minPower|body|integer|false|Sets min power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 8.|
|» » minBitrate|body|integer|false|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 5Ghz band. Can be one of '6', '9', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 12.|
|» » validAutoChannels|body|[integer]|false|Sets valid auto channels for 5Ghz band. Can be one of '36', '40', '44', '48', '52', '56', '60', '64', '100', '104', '108', '112', '116', '120', '124', '128', '132', '136', '140', '144', '149', '153', '157', '161' or '165'. Defaults to [36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 64, 100, 104, 108, 112, 116, 120, 124, 128, 132, 136, 140, 144, 149, 153, 157, 161, 165].|
|» » channelWidth|body|string|false|Sets channel width (MHz) for 5Ghz band. Can be one of 'auto', '20', '40' or '80'. Defaults to auto.|
|» » dot11ax|body|object|false|IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) settings.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 5 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Defaults to true.|
|» » rxsop|body|integer \| null|false|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|
|» sixGhzSettings|body|object|false|Settings related to 6Ghz band. Only applicable to networks with 6Ghz capable APs|
|» » maxPower|body|integer|false|Sets max power (dBm) of 6Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» » minPower|body|integer|false|Sets min power (dBm) of 6Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 8.|
|» » minBitrate|body|integer|false|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 6Ghz band. Can be one of '6', '9', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 12.|
|» » validAutoChannels|body|[integer]|false|Sets valid auto channels for 6Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '5', '9', '13', '17', '21', '25', '29', '33', '37', '41', '45', '49', '53', '57', '61', '65', '69', '73', '77', '81', '85', '89', '93', '97', '101', '105', '109', '113', '117', '121', '125', '129', '133', '137', '141', '145', '149', '153', '157', '161', '165', '169', '173', '177', '181', '185', '189', '193', '197', '201', '205', '209', '213', '217', '221', '225', '229' or '233'. Defaults to [1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 57, 61, 65, 69, 73, 77, 81, 85, 89, 93, 97, 101, 105, 109, 113, 117, 121, 125, 129, 133, 137, 141, 145, 149, 153, 157, 161, 165, 169, 173, 177, 181, 185, 189, 193, 197, 201, 205, 209, 213, 217, 221, 225, 229, 233].|

<h3 id="creates-new-rf-profile-for-this-network-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="creates-new-rf-profile-for-this-network-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The name of the new profile. Must be unique.|
|networkId|string|false|none|The network ID of the RF Profile|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the new profile. Must be unique. This param is required on creation.|
|clientBalancingEnabled|boolean|false|none|Steers client to best available access point. Can be either true or false. Defaults to true.|
|minBitrateType|string|false|none|Minimum bitrate can be set to either 'band' or 'ssid'. Defaults to band.|
|bandSelectionType|string|false|none|Band selection can be set to either 'ssid' or 'ap'. This param is required on creation.|
|apBandSettings|object|false|none|Settings that will be enabled if selectionType is set to 'ap'.|
|» bandOperationMode|string|false|none|Choice between 'dual', '2.4ghz', '5ghz', '6ghz' or 'multi'. Defaults to dual.|
|» bands|object|false|none|Settings related to all bands|
|» » enabled|[string]|false|none|List of enabled bands. Can include ["2.4", "5", "6", "disabled"]|
|» bandSteeringEnabled|boolean|false|none|Steers client to most open band. Can be either true or false. Defaults to true.|
|twoFourGhzSettings|object|false|none|Settings related to 2.4Ghz band|
|» maxPower|integer|false|none|Sets max power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» minPower|integer|false|none|Sets min power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 5.|
|» minBitrate|number(float)|false|none|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '2', '5.5', '6', '9', '11', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 11.|
|» validAutoChannels|[integer]|false|none|Sets valid auto channels for 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '6' or '11'. Defaults to [1, 6, 11].|
|» axEnabled|boolean|false|none|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Deprecated; use dot11ax.enabled instead. Defaults to true.|
|» dot11ax|object|false|none|IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) settings.|
|» » enabled|boolean|false|none|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Defaults to true.|
|» rxsop|integer \| null|false|none|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|
|fiveGhzSettings|object|false|none|Settings related to 5Ghz band|
|» maxPower|integer|false|none|Sets max power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» minPower|integer|false|none|Sets min power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 8.|
|» minBitrate|integer|false|none|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 5Ghz band. Can be one of '6', '9', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 12.|
|» validAutoChannels|[integer]|false|none|Sets valid auto channels for 5Ghz band. Can be one of '36', '40', '44', '48', '52', '56', '60', '64', '100', '104', '108', '112', '116', '120', '124', '128', '132', '136', '140', '144', '149', '153', '157', '161' or '165'. Defaults to [36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 64, 100, 104, 108, 112, 116, 120, 124, 128, 132, 136, 140, 144, 149, 153, 157, 161, 165].|
|» channelWidth|string|false|none|Sets channel width (MHz) for 5Ghz band. Can be one of 'auto', '20', '40' or '80'. Defaults to auto.|
|» rxsop|integer \| null|false|none|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|
|» dot11ax|object|false|none|IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) settings.|
|» » enabled|boolean|false|none|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 5 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Defaults to true.|
|sixGhzSettings|object|false|none|Settings related to 6Ghz band. Only applicable to networks with 6Ghz capable APs|
|» maxPower|integer|false|none|Sets max power (dBm) of 6Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» minPower|integer|false|none|Sets min power (dBm) of 6Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 8.|
|» minBitrate|integer|false|none|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 6Ghz band. Can be one of '6', '9', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 12.|
|» validAutoChannels|[integer]|false|none|Sets valid auto channels for 6Ghz band. ## Return a RF profile

<a id="opIdgetNetworkWirelessRfProfile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/wireless/rfProfiles/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/wireless/rfProfiles/{rfProfileId}`

Return a RF profile

<h3 id="return-a-rf-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|rfProfileId|path|string|true|Rf profile ID|

<h3 id="return-a-rf-profile-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-a-rf-profile-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The name of the new profile. Must be unique.|
|networkId|string|false|none|The network ID of the RF Profile|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the new profile. Must be unique. This param is required on creation.|
|clientBalancingEnabled|boolean|false|none|Steers client to best available access point. Can be either true or false. Defaults to true.|
|minBitrateType|string|false|none|Minimum bitrate can be set to either 'band' or 'ssid'. Defaults to band.|
|bandSelectionType|string|false|none|Band selection can be set to either 'ssid' or 'ap'. This param is required on creation.|
|apBandSettings|object|false|none|Settings that will be enabled if selectionType is set to 'ap'.|

<h3 id="updates-specified-rf-profile-for-this-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|rfProfileId|path|string|true|Rf profile ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the new profile. Must be unique.|
|» isIndoorDefault|body|boolean|false|Set this profile as the default indoor rf profile. If the profile ID is one of 'indoor' or 'outdoor', then a new profile will be created from the respective ID and set as the default|
|» isOutdoorDefault|body|boolean|false|Set this profile as the default outdoor rf profile. If the profile ID is one of 'indoor' or 'outdoor', then a new profile will be created from the respective ID and set as the default|
|» clientBalancingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Steers client to best available access point. Can be either true or false.|
|» minBitrateType|body|string|false|Minimum bitrate can be set to either 'band' or 'ssid'.|
|» bandSelectionType|body|string|false|Band selection can be set to either 'ssid' or 'ap'.|
|» apBandSettings|body|object|false|Settings that will be enabled if selectionType is set to 'ap'.|
|» » bandOperationMode|body|string|false|Choice between 'dual', '2.4ghz', '5ghz', '6ghz' or 'multi'.|
|» » bands|body|object|false|Settings related to all bands|
|» » » enabled|body|[string]|false|List of enabled bands. Can include ["2.4", "5", "6", "disabled"]|
|» » bandSteeringEnabled|body|boolean|false|Steers client to most open band. Can be either true or false.|
|» twoFourGhzSettings|body|object|false|Settings related to 2.4Ghz band|
|» » maxPower|body|integer|false|Sets max power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30.|
|» » minPower|body|integer|false|Sets min power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30.|
|» » minBitrate|body|number(float)|false|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '2', '5.5', '6', '9', '11', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'.|
|» » validAutoChannels|body|[integer]|false|Sets valid auto channels for 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '6' or '11'.|
|» » axEnabled|body|boolean|false|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Deprecated; use dot11ax.enabled instead.|
|» » dot11ax|body|object|false|IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) settings.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. If omitted, the existing 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.11ax setting is preserved.|
|» » rxsop|body|integer \| null|false|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|
|» fiveGhzSettings|body|object|false|Settings related to 5Ghz band|
|» » maxPower|body|integer|false|Sets max power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30.|
|» » minPower|body|integer|false|Sets min power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30.|
|» » minBitrate|body|integer|false|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 5Ghz band. Can be one of '6', '9', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'.|
|» » validAutoChannels|body|[integer]|false|Sets valid auto channels for 5Ghz band. Can be one of '36', '40', '44', '48', '52', '56', '60', '64', '100', '104', '108', '112', '116', '120', '124', '128', '132', '136', '140', '144', '149', '153', '157', '161' or '165'.|
|» » channelWidth|body|string|false|Sets channel width (MHz) for 5Ghz band. Can be one of 'auto', '20', '40' or '80'.|
|» » dot11ax|body|object|false|IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) settings.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 5 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. If omitted, the existing 5 GHz IEEE 802.11ax setting is preserved.|
|» » rxsop|body|integer \| null|false|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|
|» sixGhzSettings|body|object|false|Settings related to 6Ghz band. Only applicable to networks with 6Ghz capable APs|
|» » maxPower|body|integer|false|Sets max power (dBm) of 6Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30.|
|» » minPower|body|integer|false|Sets min power (dBm) of 6Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30.|
|» » minBitrate|body|integer|false|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 6Ghz band. Can be one of '6', '9', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'.|
|» » validAutoChannels|body|[integer]|false|Sets valid auto channels for 6Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '5', '9', '13', '17', '21', '25', '29', '33', '37', '41', '45', '49', '53', '57', '61', '65', '69', '73', '77', '81', '85', '89', '93', '97', '101', '105', '109', '113', '117', '121', '125', '129', '133', '137', '141', '145', '149', '153', '157', '161', '165', '169', '173', '177', '181', '185', '189', '193', '197', '201', '205', '209', '213', '217', '221', '225', '229' or '233'.|
|» » channelWidth|body|string|false|Sets channel width (MHz) for 6Ghz band. Can be one of 'auto', '20', '40', '80', '160' or '320'.|
|» » rxsop|body|integer \| null|false|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="updates-specified-rf-profile-for-this-network-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|The name of the new profile. Must be unique.|
|networkId|string|false|none|The network ID of the RF Profile|
|name|string|false|none|The name of the new profile. Must be unique. This param is required on creation.|
|clientBalancingEnabled|boolean|false|none|Steers client to best available access point. Can be either true or false. Defaults to true.|
|minBitrateType|string|false|none|Minimum bitrate can be set to either 'band' or 'ssid'. Defaults to band.|
|bandSelectionType|string|false|none|Band selection can be set to either 'ssid' or 'ap'. This param is required on creation.|
|apBandSettings|object|false|none|Settings that will be enabled if selectionType is set to 'ap'.|
|» bandOperationMode|string|false|none|Choice between 'dual', '2.4ghz', '5ghz', '6ghz' or 'multi'. Defaults to dual.|
|» bands|object|false|none|Settings related to all bands|
|» » enabled|[string]|false|none|List of enabled bands. Can include ["2.4", "5", "6", "disabled"]|
|» bandSteeringEnabled|boolean|false|none|Steers client to most open band. Can be either true or false. Defaults to true.|
|twoFourGhzSettings|object|false|none|Settings related to 2.4Ghz band|
|» maxPower|integer|false|none|Sets max power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» minPower|integer|false|none|Sets min power (dBm) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 5.|
|» minBitrate|number(float)|false|none|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '2', '5.5', '6', '9', '11', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 11.|
|» validAutoChannels|[integer]|false|none|Sets valid auto channels for 2.4Ghz band. Can be one of '1', '6' or '11'. Defaults to [1, 6, 11].|
|» axEnabled|boolean|false|none|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Deprecated; use dot11ax.enabled instead. Defaults to true.|
|» dot11ax|object|false|none|IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) settings.|
|» » enabled|boolean|false|none|Determines whether IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) on the 2.4 GHz band is enabled. Can be either true or false. If false, we highly recommend disabling band steering. Defaults to true.|
|» rxsop|integer \| null|false|none|The RX-SOP level controls the sensitivity of the radio. It is strongly recommended to use RX-SOP only after consulting a wireless expert. RX-SOP can be configured in the range of -65 to -95 (dBm). A value of null will reset this to the default.|
|fiveGhzSettings|object|false|none|Settings related to 5Ghz band|
|» maxPower|integer|false|none|Sets max power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 30.|
|» minPower|integer|false|none|Sets min power (dBm) of 5Ghz band. Can be integer between 2 and 30. Defaults to 8.|
|» minBitrate|integer|false|none|Sets min bitrate (Mbps) of 5Ghz band. Can be one of '6', '9', '12', '18', '24', '36', '48' or '54'. Defaults to 12.|
|» validAutoChannels|[integer]|false|none|Sets valid auto channels for 5Ghz band. Can be one of '36', '40', '44', '48', '52', '56', '60', '64', '100', '104', '108', '112', '116', '120', '124', '128', '132', '136', '140', '144', '149', '153', '157', '161' or '165'. ```

`DELETE /networks/{networkId}/wireless/rfProfiles/{rfProfileId}`

Delete a RF Profile
