## Update quality and retention settings for the given camera

<a id="opIdupdateDeviceCameraQualityAndRetention"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/camera/qualityAndRetention \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "profileId": "1234",
    "motionBasedRetentionEnabled": false,
    "audioRecordingEnabled": false,
    "restrictedBandwidthModeEnabled": false,
    "quality": "Standard",
    "resolution": "1280x720",
    "motionDetectorVersion": 2
  }'
```

`PUT /devices/{serial}/camera/qualityAndRetention`

Update quality and retention settings for the given camera

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "profileId": "1234",
  "motionBasedRetentionEnabled": false,
  "audioRecordingEnabled": false,
  "restrictedBandwidthModeEnabled": false,
  "quality": "Standard",
  "resolution": "1280x720",
  "motionDetectorVersion": 2
}
```

<h3 id="update-quality-and-retention-settings-for-the-given-camera-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» profileId|body|string \| null|false|The ID of a quality and retention profile to assign to the camera. The profile's settings will override all of the per-camera quality and retention settings. If the value of this parameter is null, any existing profile will be unassigned from the camera.|
|» motionBasedRetentionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating if motion-based retention is enabled(true) or disabled(false) on the camera.|
|» audioRecordingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating if audio recording is enabled(true) or disabled(false) on the camera|
|» restrictedBandwidthModeEnabled|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating if restricted bandwidth is enabled(true) or disabled(false) on the camera. This setting does not apply to MV2 cameras.|
|» quality|body|string|false|Quality of the camera. Can be one of 'Standard', 'High', 'Enhanced' or 'Ultra'. Not all qualities are supported by every camera model.|
|» resolution|body|string|false|Resolution of the camera. Can be one of '1280x720', '1920x1080', '1080x1080', '2112x2112', '2880x2880', '2688x1512' or '3840x2160'.Not all resolutions are supported by every camera model.|
|» motionDetectorVersion|body|integer|false|The version of the motion detector that will be used by the camera. Only applies to Gen 2 cameras. Defaults to v2.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» quality|Enhanced|
|» quality|High|
|» quality|Standard|
|» quality|Ultra|
|» resolution|1080x1080|
|» resolution|1280x720|
|» resolution|1920x1080|
|» resolution|2112x2112|
|» resolution|2688x1512|
|» resolution|2880x2880|
|» resolution|3840x2160|
|» motionDetectorVersion|1|
|» motionDetectorVersion|2|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "profileId": "1234",
  "motionBasedRetentionEnabled": false,
  "audioRecordingEnabled": false,
  "restrictedBandwidthModeEnabled": false,
  "quality": "Standard",
  "resolution": "1280x720",
  "motionDetectorVersion": 2
}
```

<h3 id="update-quality-and-retention-settings-for-the-given-camera-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="update-quality-and-retention-settings-for-the-given-camera-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|profileId|string \| null|false|none|Quality and retention profile ID; null if not using a profile|
|motionBasedRetentionEnabled|boolean|false|none|Whether motion-based retention is enabled|
|audioRecordingEnabled|boolean|false|none|Whether audio recording is enabled|

|» » secondary|body|string \| null|true|The id of the secondary wireless profile|

## Creates new quality retention profile for this network.

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkCameraQualityRetentionProfile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/camera/qualityRetentionProfiles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "name": "Sample quality retention profile"
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/camera/qualityRetentionProfiles`

Creates new quality retention profile for this network.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Sample quality retention profile"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-new-quality-retention-profile-for-this-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new profile. Must be unique. This parameter is required.|
|» motionBasedRetentionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Deletes footage older than 3 days in which no motion was detected. Can be either true or false. Defaults to false. This setting does not apply to MV2 cameras.|
|» restrictedBandwidthModeEnabled|body|boolean|false|Disable features that require additional bandwidth such as Motion Recap. Can be either true or false. Defaults to false. This setting does not apply to MV2 cameras.|
|» audioRecordingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to record audio. Can be either true or false. Defaults to false.|
|» cloudArchiveEnabled|body|boolean|false|Create redundant video backup using Cloud Archive. Can be either true or false. Defaults to false.|
|» motionDetectorVersion|body|integer|false|The version of the motion detector that will be used by the camera. Only applies to Gen 2 cameras. Defaults to v2.|
|» smartRetention|body|object|false|Smart Retention records footage in two qualities and intelligently retains higher quality when motion, people or vehicles are detected.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating if Smart Retention is enabled(true) or disabled(false).|
|» scheduleId|body|string \| null|false|Schedule for which this camera will record video, or 'null' to always record.|
|» maxRetentionDays|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of days for which the data will be stored, or 'null' to keep data until storage space runs out. If the former, it can be in the range of one to ninety days.|

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the new profile. Must be unique.|
|» motionBasedRetentionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Deletes footage older than 3 days in which no motion was detected. Can be either true or false. Defaults to false. This setting does not apply to MV2 cameras.|

|» smartRetention|body|object|false|Smart Retention records footage in two qualities and intelligently retains higher quality when motion, people or vehicles are detected.|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|boundaryIds|query|[string]|true|A list of boundary ids. The returned cameras will be filtered to only include these ids.|
|ranges|query|[object]|true|A list of time ranges with intervals|
|duration|query|integer|false|The minimum time, in seconds, that the person or car remains in the area to be counted. Defaults to boundary configuration or 60.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 1 - 1000. Defaults to 1000.|
|boundaryTypes|query|[string]|false|The detection types. Defaults to 'person'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|boundaryTypes|person|
|boundaryTypes|vehicle|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "boundaryId": "k74272e",
    "type": "line",
    "results": {
      "startTime": "2018-02-11T00:00:00Z",
      "endTime": "2018-05-12T00:00:00Z",
      "objectType": "person",
      "in": 22,
      "out": 13
    }
  }
]
```

<h3 id="returns-analytics-data-for-timespans-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="returns-analytics-data-for-timespans-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» boundaryId|string|false|none|The boundary id|
|» type|string|false|none|The boundary type|
|» results|object|false|none|The analytics data|
|» » startTime|string|false|none|The period start time|
|» » endTime|string|false|none|The period end time|
|» » objectType|string|false|none|The detection type|
|» » in|integer|false|none|The number of detections entered|
|» » out|integer|false|none|The number of detections exited|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: camera:config:read )

## Return the performance score for a single Secure Appliance or Secure Router

<a id="opIdgetDeviceAppliancePerformance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/appliance/performance \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /devices/{serial}/appliance/performance`

Return the performance score for a single Secure Appliance or Secure Router. Only primary Secure Appliance devices supported. If no data is available, a 204 error code is returned.

<h3 id="return-the-performance-score-for-a-single-secure-appliance-or-secure-router-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 30 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 14 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be greater than or equal to 30 minutes and be less than or equal to 14 days. The default is 30 minutes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "perfScore": 10
}
```

<h3 id="return-the-performance-score-for-a-single-secure-appliance-or-secure-router-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-the-performance-score-for-a-single-secure-appliance-or-secure-router-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|perfScore|number(float)|false|none|Utilization for the device|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: sdwan:telemetry:read )
</aside>

```json
      "targetPower": 15
    }
```
```bash
  }'
```

## Generate a new vMX authentication token

<a id="opIdcreateDeviceApplianceVmxAuthenticationToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/appliance/vmx/authenticationToken \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /devices/{serial}/appliance/vmx/authenticationToken`

Generate a new vMX authentication token

<h3 id="generate-a-new-vmx-authentication-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "token": "ffc0b7b578b61be5bd1d172132c78044/9af03bd84d474",
  "expiresAt": "2021-06-18T12:40:10Z"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-new-vmx-authentication-token-responses">Responses</h3>

## List the security events for a client

<a id="opIdgetNetworkApplianceClientSecurityEvents"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/appliance/clients/string/security/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networks/{networkId}/appliance/clients/{clientId}/security/events`

List the security events for a client. Clients can be identified by a client key or either the MAC or IP depending on whether the network uses Track-by-IP.

<h3 id="list-the-security-events-for-a-client-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|clientId|path|string|true|Client ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. Data is gathered after the specified t0 value. The maximum lookback period is 791 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 791 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 791 days. The default is 31 days.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 100.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sorted order of security events based on event detection time. Order options are 'ascending' or 'descending'. Default is ascending order.|

|---|---|
|sortOrder|ascending|
|sortOrder|descending|

```json
  },
```

|» » id|body|string|true|The identifier of an existing custom intrusion policy in this organization|

|» » useDefault|body|boolean|true|true/false whether to use special IPv4 addresses: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5735 (required). Default value is true if none currently saved|
|» » includedCidr|body|[string]|false|list of IP addresses or subnets being protected (required if 'useDefault' is false)|
|» » excludedCidr|body|[string]|false|list of IP addresses or subnets being excluded from protection (required if 'useDefault' is false)|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|detection|

|» idsRulesets|balanced|
|» idsRulesets|connectivity|
|» idsRulesets|security|

## Update the attributes of an MX SSID

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkApplianceSsid"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/appliance/ssids/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My SSID",
    "enabled": true,
    "defaultVlanId": 1,
    "authMode": "8021x-radius",
    "psk": "psk",
    "radiusServers": [
      {
        "host": "0.0.0.0",
        "port": 1000,
        "secret": "secret"
      }
    ],
    "encryptionMode": "wpa",
    "wpaEncryptionMode": "WPA2 only",
    "visible": true,
    "dhcpEnforcedDeauthentication": {
      "enabled": true
    },
    "dot11w": {
      "enabled": true,
      "required": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /networks/{networkId}/appliance/ssids/{number}`

Update the attributes of an MX SSID

```json
  "name": "My SSID",
  "enabled": true,
  "defaultVlanId": 1,
  "authMode": "8021x-radius",
  "psk": "psk",
  "radiusServers": [
    {
      "host": "0.0.0.0",
      "port": 1000,
      "secret": "secret"
    }
  ],
  "encryptionMode": "wpa",
  "wpaEncryptionMode": "WPA2 only",
  "visible": true,
  "dhcpEnforcedDeauthentication": {
    "enabled": true
  },
  "dot11w": {
    "enabled": true,
    "required": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-attributes-of-an-mx-ssid-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|number|path|string|true|Number|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the SSID.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether or not the SSID is enabled.|
|» defaultVlanId|body|integer|false|The VLAN ID of the VLAN associated to this SSID. This parameter is only valid if the network is in routed mode.|
|» authMode|body|string|false|The association control method for the SSID ('open', 'psk', '8021x-meraki', '8021x-radius' or '8021x-nac').|
|» psk|body|string|false|The passkey for the SSID. This param is only valid if the authMode is 'psk'.|
|» radiusServers|body|[object]|false|The RADIUS 802.1x servers to be used for authentication. This param is only valid if the authMode is '8021x-radius'.|
|» » host|body|string|false|The IP address of your RADIUS server.|
|» » port|body|integer|false|The UDP port your RADIUS servers listens on for Access-requests.|
|» » secret|body|string|false|The RADIUS client shared secret.|
|» encryptionMode|body|string|false|The psk encryption mode for the SSID ('wep' or 'wpa'). This param is only valid if the authMode is 'psk'.|
|» wpaEncryptionMode|body|string|false|The types of WPA encryption. ('WPA1 and WPA2', 'WPA2 only', 'WPA3 Transition Mode' or 'WPA3 only'). This param is only valid if (1) the authMode is 'psk' & the encryptionMode is 'wpa' OR (2) the authMode is '8021x-meraki' OR (3) the authMode is '8021x-radius' OR (4) the authMode is '8021x-nac'|
|» visible|body|boolean|false|Boolean indicating whether the MX should advertise or hide this SSID.|
|» dhcpEnforcedDeauthentication|body|object|false|DHCP Enforced Deauthentication enables the disassociation of wireless clients in addition to Mandatory DHCP. This param is only valid on firmware versions >= MX 17.0 where the associated LAN has Mandatory DHCP Enabled |
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enable DCHP Enforced Deauthentication on the SSID.|
|» dot11w|body|object|false|The current setting for Protected Management Frames (802.11w).|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether 802.11w is enabled or not.|
|» » required|body|boolean|false|(Optional) Whether 802.11w is required or not.|

|» authMode|8021x-nac|
|» authMode|8021x-radius|
|» authMode|open|
|» authMode|psk|
|» encryptionMode|wep|
|» encryptionMode|wpa|
|» wpaEncryptionMode|WPA1 and WPA2|
|» wpaEncryptionMode|WPA2 only|
|» wpaEncryptionMode|WPA3 Transition Mode|
|» wpaEncryptionMode|WPA3 only|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|defaultRulesEnabled|boolean|false|none|Whether default traffic shaping rules are enabled (true) or disabled (false). There are 4 default rules, which can be seen on your network's traffic shaping page. Note that default rules count against the rule limit of 8.|

|» definitions|[object]|true|none|    A list of objects describing the definitions of your traffic shaping rule. At least one definition is required.<br>|
|» » type|string|true|none|    The type of definition. Can be one of 'application', 'applicationCategory', 'host', 'port', 'ipRange', 'localNet', 'source', 'source_port', 'destination' or 'destination_port'.<br>    Security Appliance networks support 'host', 'port', 'ipRange', 'localNet', 'application', and 'applicationCategory'.<br>    Secure Router networks support 'source', 'source_port', 'destination', 'destination_port', 'application', and 'applicationCategory'.<br>|
|» » value|string|true|none|    If "type" is 'host', 'port', 'ipRange' or 'localNet', then "value" must be a string, matching either<br>    a hostname (e.g. "somesite.com"), a port (e.g. 8080), or an IP range ("192.1.0.0",<br>    "192.1.0.0/16", or "10.1.0.0/16:80"). 'localNet' also supports CIDR notation, excluding<br>    custom ports.<br>    If "type" is 'source', 'source_port', 'destination' or 'destination_port', then "value" must be a string:<br>    for 'source' and 'destination', the string must be an IPv4 address or CIDR with optional port<br>    information (e.g. "192.1.0.0", "192.1.0.0/16", "10.1.0.0/16:80", "10.1.0.0/16:80-90");<br>    for 'source_port' and 'destination_port', the string must be a single port or port range (e.g. 8080, 8000-9000).<br>    If "type" is 'application' or 'applicationCategory', then "value" must be an object<br>    with the structure { "id": "meraki:layer7/..." }, where "id" is the application category or<br>    application ID (for a list of IDs for your network, use the trafficShaping/applicationCategories<br>    endpoint).<br>|
|» perClientBandwidthLimits|object|false|none|    An object describing the bandwidth settings for your rule.<br>|
|» » settings|string|false|none|    How bandwidth limits are applied by your rule. Can be one of 'network default', 'ignore' or 'custom'.<br>    Secure Router networks support only the 'ignore' setting.<br>|
|» » bandwidthLimits|object|false|none|The bandwidth limits object, specifying the upload ('limitUp') and download ('limitDown') speed in Kbps. These are only enforced if 'settings' is set to 'custom'.|
|» » » limitUp|integer|false|none|The maximum upload limit (integer, in Kbps).|
|» » » limitDown|integer|false|none|The maximum download limit (integer, in Kbps).|
|» dscpTagValue|integer \| null|false|none|    The DSCP tag applied by your rule. null means 'Do not change DSCP tag'.<br>    For a list of possible tag values, use the trafficShaping/dscpTaggingOptions endpoint.<br>|
|» priority|string|false|none|    A string, indicating the priority level for packets bound to your rule.<br>    Can be 'low', 'normal' or 'high'. This field is supported for Security Appliance networks.<br>|

## Update VPN exclusion rules for an MX network.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/appliance/trafficShaping/vpnExclusions \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
```

|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 30 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 10 minutes.|
|resolution|query|integer|false|The time resolution in seconds for returned data. The valid resolutions are: 60, 300, 600, 1800, 3600, 86400. The default is 60.|

```json
]
```

## Add a VLAN

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkApplianceVlan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/appliance/vlans \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "1234",
    "name": "My VLAN",
    "subnet": "192.168.1.0/24",
    "applianceIp": "192.168.1.2",

    "templateVlanType": "same",
    "cidr": "192.168.1.0/24",
    "mask": 28,
    "ipv6": {
      "enabled": true,
      "prefixAssignments": [
        {
          "autonomous": false,
          "disabled": false,
          "staticPrefix": "2001:db8:3c4d:15::/64",
          "staticApplianceIp6": "2001:db8:3c4d:15::1",
          "origin": {
            "type": "internet",
            "interfaces": [
              "wan0"
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "dhcpHandling": "Run a DHCP server",
    "dhcpRelayServerIps": [
      "192.168.1.0",
      "192.168.128.0"
    ],
    "dhcpLeaseTime": "30 minutes",
    "mandatoryDhcp": {
      "enabled": true
    },
    "dhcpBootOptionsEnabled": true,
    "dhcpBootNextServer": "1.2.3.4",
    "dhcpBootFilename": "sample.file",
    "dhcpOptions": [
      {
        "code": "3",
        "type": "text",
        "value": "five"
      }
    ],
    "sgt": {
      "id": 1234
    },
    "vrf": {
      "id": "1000"
    },
    "uplinks": [
      {
        "interface": "wan1",
        "nat": {
          "enabled": true
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

<h3 id="update-a-hub-bgp-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Boolean value to enable or disable the BGP configuration. When BGP is enabled, the asNumber (ASN) will be autopopulated with the preconfigured ASN at other Hubs or a default value if there is no ASN configured.|
|» asNumber|body|integer|false|An Autonomous System Number (ASN) is required if you are to run BGP and peer with another BGP Speaker outside of the Auto VPN domain. This ASN will be applied to the entire Auto VPN domain and is only configurable for Auto VPN BGP networks. The entire 4-byte ASN range is supported. So, the ASN must be an integer between 1 and 4294967295. When absent, this field is not updated. If no value exists then it defaults to 64512.|
|» ibgpHoldTimer|body|integer|false|The iBGP holdtimer in seconds. The iBGP holdtimer must be an integer between 12 and 240. When absent, this field is not updated. If no value exists then it defaults to 240.|
|» ipv6|body|object|false|Settings for IPv6 configurations on the organization.|
|» » singlePeering|body|object|false|Settings for IPv6 single peering.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether a single IPv6 BGP peer is enabled.|
|» tunnelDownTermination|body|object|false|Settings for tunnel down termination on the organization.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether tunnel down termination is enabled.|
|» localAsNumber|body|integer \| null|false|Network-specific local Autonomous System Number (ASN) to which the appliance belongs. This field is only configurable for Independent BGP networks.|
|» priorityRoute|body|string|false|Sets the priority route between eBGP and Auto VPN.|
|» routerId|body|string \| null|false|The router ID of the appliance|
|» neighbors|body|[object]|false|List of BGP neighbors. This list replaces the existing set of neighbors. When absent, this field is not updated.|
|» » ip|body|string|false|The IPv4 address of the neighbor|
|» » ipv6|body|object|false|Information regarding IPv6 address of the neighbor, Required if `ip` is not present.|
|» » » address|body|string|true|The IPv6 address of the neighbor.|
|» » remoteAsNumber|body|integer|true|Remote ASN of the neighbor. The remote ASN must be an integer between 1 and 4294967295.|
|» » receiveLimit|body|integer|false|The receive limit is the maximum number of routes that can be received from any BGP peer. The receive limit must be an integer between 0 and 2147483647. When absent, it defaults to 0.|
|» » allowTransit|body|boolean|false|When this feature is on, the Meraki device will advertise routes learned from other Autonomous Systems, thereby allowing traffic between Autonomous Systems to transit this AS. When absent, it defaults to false.|
|» » ebgpHoldTimer|body|integer|true|The eBGP hold timer in seconds for each neighbor. The eBGP hold timer must be an integer between 12 and 240.|
|» » ebgpMultihop|body|integer|true|Configure this if the neighbor is not adjacent. The eBGP multi-hop must be an integer between 1 and 255.|
|» » sourceInterface|body|string|false|The output interface for peering with the remote BGP peer. Valid values are: 'wan{NUMBER}' (e.g. 'wan3') or 'vlan{VLAN ID}' (e.g. 'vlan123') for MX; 'l3lan{ID}' (e.g. 'l3lan123') or an eligible 'wan{NUMBER}' for Secure/Catalyst Router. Secure/Catalyst Router WAN interfaces must be enabled, non-cellular uplinks on supported AutoVPN hub networks. NAT and no-NAT uplinks are supported.|
|» » nextHopIp|body|string|false|The IPv4 address of the remote BGP peer that will establish a TCP session with the local MX.|
|» » ttlSecurity|body|object|false|Settings for BGP TTL security to protect BGP peering sessions from forged IP attacks.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Boolean value to enable or disable BGP TTL security.|
|» » authentication|body|object|false|Authentication settings between BGP peers.|
|» » » password|body|string|false|Password to configure MD5 authentication between BGP peers.|
|» » multiExitDiscriminator|body|integer|false|Configures the local metric associated with routes received from the remote peer. Routes from peers with lower metrics are will be preferred. Must be an integer between 0 and 4294967295. MED is 6th in the decision tree when identical routes from multiple peers exist.|
|» » pathPrepend|body|[integer]|false|Prepends the AS_PATH BGP Attribute associated with routes received from the remote peer. Configurable value of ASNs to prepend. Length of the array may not exceed 10, and each ASN in the array must be an integer between 1 and 4294967295. AS_PATH is 4th in the decision tree when identical routes from multiple peers exist.|
|» » weight|body|integer|false|Sets the local weight for routes received from the remote peer. Routes from peers with higher weights will be preferred. Must be an integer between 0 and 49 for Secure Appliance or between 0 and 65535 for Secure Router.|
|» » filterIn|body|[string]|false|Filters routes received from an eBGP neighbor. Each entry must be an IPv4 CIDR string (e.g., '10.0.0.0/8' or '10.0.0.5/32').|
|» » filter|body|object|false|Filters routes received from an eBGP neighbor.|
|» » » out|body|[string]|false|Filters routes advertised to an eBGP neighbor. Each entry must be an IPv4 CIDR string (e.g., '10.0.0.0/8' or '10.0.0.5/32').|
|» » communityOut|body|[string]|false|List of BGP communities tagged to the routes advertised to an eBGP neighbor.|
|» » explicitOutboundRouteAdvertisement|body|object \| null|false|Settings for explicit outbound route advertisement to an eBGP neighbor.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether explicit outbound routes are advertised to the eBGP neighbor.|

## Update the site-to-site VPN settings of an MX network or configuration template in NAT mode

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/appliance/vpn/siteToSiteVpn \
  -X PUT \

  -d '{
    "confirmed": false,
    "mode": "spoke",
    "natTraversal": {
      "mode": "manual",
      "publicIp": "203.0.113.8",
      "publicPort": 4500
    },
    "hubs": [
      {
        "hubId": "N_4901849",
        "useDefaultRoute": true
      }
    ],
    "subnets": [
      {
        "localSubnet": "192.168.1.0/24",
        "useVpn": true,
        "nat": {
          "enabled": true,
          "remoteSubnet": "198.51.100.3/32"
        }
      }
    ],
    "sgt": {
      "enabled": true
    },
    "subnet": {
      "nat": {
        "isAllowed": true
      }
    },
    "hostTranslations": [
      {
        "name": "Host 1",
        "local": {
          "address": "192.168.1.10"
        },
        "remote": {
          "address": "72.168.2.10"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /networks/{networkId}/appliance/vpn/siteToSiteVpn`

Update the site-to-site VPN settings of an MX network or configuration template in NAT mode. Unacknowledged warnings return 400 Bad Request with retry guidance in errors and the warnings in confirmations. Review the warnings returned in confirmations, then retry with confirmed: true to accept them. Fatal errors must be corrected before retrying.

This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

<h3 id="returns-packet-counter-overviews-for-all-interfaces-on-secure-routers-in-the-organization-including-totals-and-average-rates-by-packet-type-over-the-requested-timespan-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» » subslot|integer \| null|false|none|Optional subslot number for this interface, if applicable.|

Note: results may be approximate because packet counter aggregated records may not align exactly with the requested timespan. Recent/current data may be incomplete because aggregated data is refreshed periodically, which can introduce latency.|
|» » » type|string|false|none|Packet type. 3 packet types exist: broadcast, unicast, and multicast. "broadcast unicast multicast" is the sum of all 3 packet types. Other values denote error or size conditions.|
|» » » total|integer|false|none|The total count of sent and received packets during the timespan.|
|» » » sent|integer|false|none|The total count of packets sent during the timespan.|
|» » » recv|integer|false|none|The total count of packets received during the timespan.|
|» » » rates|object|false|none|Packets per second rates during the timespan.|
|» » » » average|object|false|none|Average rates during the timespan.|
|» » » » » total|number(float)|false|none|The rate of all packets sent and received during the timespan.|
|» » » » » sent|number(float)|false|none|The rate of packets sent during the timespan.|
|» » » » » recv|number(float)|false|none|The rate of packets received during the timespan.|

## Show VPN history stats for networks in an organization

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/appliance/vpn/stats`

Show VPN history stats for networks in an organization. The usageSummary values are derived from 20-minute aggregate data. For accurate usageSummary values, use query windows of at least 20 minutes. Shorter or very recent windows may return 0 until aggregate data is available.

<h3 id="show-vpn-history-stats-for-networks-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 300. Default is 300.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|networkIds|query|[string]|false|A list of Meraki network IDs to filter results to contain only specified networks. E.g.: networkIds[]=N_12345678&networkIds[]=L_3456|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 31 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 31 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 31 days. The default is 1 day.|

|» » childLifetime|integer|false|none|The lifetime of the Phase 2 SA in seconds.|

|» » » enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether BGP TTL security is enabled. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above|
|» » authentication|object|false|none|Authentication settings between BGP peers. Supported only for MX 26.2 and above|

|» group|object|false|none|[optional] Contains the mapping between primary tunnel and backup tunnels.|

|» » failover|object|false|none|[optional] Contains the failover configuration for the group.|
|» » » directToInternet|boolean|false|none|[optional] When both primary and backup tunnels are down, direct traffic to the internet. Traffic will be routed via the WAN|
|» » activeActiveTunnel|boolean|false|none|[optional] Both primary and backup tunnels are active.|

## Update the third party VPN peers for an organization

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationApplianceVpnThirdPartyVPNPeers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/appliance/vpn/thirdPartyVPNPeers \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "peers": [
      {
        "peerId": "1234",
        "name": "Peer Name",
        "publicIp": "123.123.123.1",
        "publicHostname": "example.com",
        "privateSubnets": [
          "192.168.1.0/24",
          "192.168.128.0/24"
        ],
        "localId": "myMXId@meraki.com",
        "remoteId": "miles@meraki.com",
        "ipsecPolicies": {
          "ikeCipherAlgo": [
            "tripledes"
          ],
          "ikeAuthAlgo": [
            "sha1"
          ],
          "ikePrfAlgo": [
            "prfsha1"
          ],
          "ikeDiffieHellmanGroup": [
            "group2"
          ],
          "ikeLifetime": 28800,
          "childCipherAlgo": [
            "aes128"
          ],
          "childAuthAlgo": [
            "sha1"
          ],
          "childPfsGroup": [
            "disabled"
          ],
          "childLifetime": 28800
        },
        "ipsecPoliciesPreset": "default (insecure)",
        "slaPolicy": {
          "id": "1234"
        },
        "secret": "Sample Password",
        "ikeVersion": "2",
        "networkTags": [
          "none"
        ],
        "network": {
          "ids": [
            "N_1",
            "L_2",
            "N_3"
          ]
        },
        "isRouteBased": true,
        "ebgpNeighbor": {
          "neighborIp": "10.10.10.22",
          "ipVersion": 4,
          "remoteAsNumber": 64343,
          "ebgpHoldTimer": 180,
          "ebgpMultihop": 2,
          "sourceIp": "10.10.10.22",
          "vrf": {
            "id": "12345",
            "name": "VRF Blue"
          },
          "pathPrepend": [
            1,
            2
          ],
          "multiExitDiscriminator": 1,
          "weight": 10
        },
        "ecmpUplinkConfigs": [
          {
            "id": "7890",
            "wan": "WAN 1",

              "169.254.10.0/30"
            ],

              "neighborIp": "169.254.10.2",
              "sourceIp": "169.254.10.1"
            }
          }

        "priorityInGroup": 1,
        "group": {
          "number": 1,
          "failover": {
            "directToInternet": true
          },
          "activeActiveTunnel": true
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organizationId}/appliance/vpn/thirdPartyVPNPeers`

Update the third party VPN peers for an organization.

Subnet overlap warning: Unlike the Dashboard UI, updateOrganizationApplianceVpnThirdPartyVPNPeers does not run the org-wide subnet-overlap validation before saving changes. Requests with overlapping VPN subnets will succeed through the API, but the resulting configuration may be blocked from further edits in Dashboard until the overlaps are resolved manually. Use this endpoint only when you've already confirmed the advertised subnets are unique across the organization.


`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/appliance/vpn/vpnFirewallRules`

Return the firewall rules for an organization's site-to-site VPN

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "comment": "Allow TCP traffic to subnet with HTTP servers.",
      "policy": "allow",
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "srcPort": "Any",
      "srcCidr": "Any",
      "destPort": "443",
      "destCidr": "192.168.1.0/24",
      "syslogEnabled": false
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="return-the-firewall-rules-for-an-organizations-site-to-site-vpn-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rules|[object]|false|none|An ordered array of the firewall rules (not including the default rule)|
|» comment|string|false|none|Description of the rule (optional)|
|» policy|string|false|none|'allow' or 'deny' traffic specified by this rule|
|» protocol|string|false|none|The type of protocol (must be 'tcp', 'udp', 'icmp', 'icmp6' or 'any')|
|» srcPort|string|false|none|Comma-separated list of source port(s) (integer in the range 1-65535), or 'any'|
|» srcCidr|string|false|none|Comma-separated list of source IP address(es) (in IP or CIDR notation), or 'any' (note: FQDN not supported for source addresses)|
|» destPort|string|false|none|Comma-separated list of destination port(s) (integer in the range 1-65535), or 'any'|
|» destCidr|string|false|none|Comma-separated list of destination IP address(es) (in IP or CIDR notation), fully-qualified domain names (FQDN) or 'any'|
|» syslogEnabled|boolean|false|none|Log this rule to syslog (true or false, boolean value) - only applicable if a syslog has been configured (optional)|

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/switch/ports/cycle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
```

## Return the packet counters for all the ports of a switch

<a id="opIdgetDeviceSwitchPortsStatusesPackets"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/switch/ports/statuses/packets \
```

`GET /devices/{serial}/switch/ports/statuses/packets`

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The value is used only to determine the elapsed duration between t0 and the time of the request; the API snaps that duration to the nearest preset window (5 minutes, 15 minutes, 1 hour, or 1 day).|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify t0. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 86400 seconds (1 day). The default is 1 day.|

```json
          "total": 1,
          "sent": 1,
          "recv": 0
        }
      }
    ]
  }
```

|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="return-the-packet-counters-for-all-the-ports-of-a-switch-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» portId|string|false|none|The string identifier of this port on the switch. This is commonly just the port number but may contain additional identifying information such as the slot and module-type if the port is located on a port module.|
|» packets|[object]|false|none|The packet counts on the switch. Note that this data is collected periodically from the switch. Any data from the past five minutes may be incomplete.|
|» » desc|string|false|none|The type of packets being counted.|
|» » total|integer|false|none|The total count of sent and received packets.|
|» » sent|integer|false|none|The total count of packets sent by the switch during the timespan.|
|» » recv|integer|false|none|The total count of packets received by the switch during the timespan.|
|» » ratePerSec|object|false|none|Packet rates measured in packets per second.|
|» » » total|integer|false|none|The rate of all packets sent and received during the timespan|
|» » » sent|integer|false|none|The rate of packets sent during the timespan|

<h3 id="create-a-layer-3-interface-for-a-switch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A friendly name or description for the interface or VLAN (max length 128 characters).|
|» mode|body|string|false|L3 Interface mode, can be one of 'vlan', 'routed', 'loopback', or 'oob_management'. Default is 'vlan'. IOS XE firmware 17.18 or higher is required for 'routed' mode; IOS XE firmware 26.1.2 or higher is required for 'oob_management' mode.|
|» subnet|body|string \| null|false|The network that this L3 interface is on, in CIDR notation (ex. 10.1.1.0/24).|
|» switchPortId|body|string \| null|false|Switch Port ID when in Routed mode (IOS XE firmware 17.18 or higher required)|
|» interfaceIp|body|string \| null|false|The IP address that will be used for Layer 3 routing on this VLAN or subnet. This cannot be the same         as the device management IP.|
|» mtu|body|integer \| null|false|The interface MTU. Applies to native switch layer 3 interfaces, including VLAN and routed modes.|
|» multicastRouting|body|string|false|Enable multicast support if, multicast routing between VLANs is required. Options are:         'disabled', 'enabled' or 'IGMP snooping querier'. Default is 'disabled'.|
|» vlanId|body|integer \| null|false|The VLAN this L3 interface is on. VLAN must be between 1 and 4094.|
|» defaultGateway|body|string|false|The next hop for any traffic that isn't going to a directly connected subnet or over a static route.         This IP address must exist in a subnet with a L3 interface. Required if this is the first IPv4 interface.|
|» ospfSettings|body|object|false|The OSPF routing settings of the interface.|
|» » area|body|string|false|The OSPF area to which this interface should belong. Can be either 'disabled' or the identifier of an           existing OSPF area. Defaults to 'disabled'.|
|» » cost|body|integer|false|The path cost for this interface. Defaults to 1, but can be increased up to 65535           to give lower priority.|
|» » isPassiveEnabled|body|boolean|false|When enabled, OSPF will not run on the interface, but the subnet will still be advertised.|
|» » networkType|body|string|false|OSPF network type|
|» ipv6|body|object|false|The IPv6 settings of the interface.|
|» » assignmentMode|body|string \| null|false|The IPv6 assignment mode for the interface. Can be either 'eui-64' or 'static'.|
|» » prefix|body|string \| null|false|The IPv6 prefix of the interface. Required if IPv6 object is included.|
|» » address|body|string \| null|false|The IPv6 address of the interface. Required if assignmentMode is 'static'. Must not be included if           assignmentMode is 'eui-64'.|
|» » gateway|body|string|false|The IPv6 default gateway of the interface. Required if prefix is defined and this is the first           interface with IPv6 configured.|
|» vrf|body|object|false|The VRF settings of the interface. Requires IOS XE 17.18 or higher|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the VRF this interface belongs to.|
|» loopback|body|object|false|The loopback settings of the interface.|
|» bidirectionalForwardingDetection|body|object|false|BFD configuration for the L3 interface.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether BFD is enabled on the L3 interface.|
|» » intervalInterface|body|object|false|BFD interval configuration for the L3 interface.|
|» » » msecs|body|integer \| null|false|BFD transmit interval in milliseconds.|
|» » » minRx|body|integer \| null|false|Minimum BFD receive interval in milliseconds.|
|» » » multiplier|body|integer \| null|false|BFD detection multiplier.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|interfaceId|path|string|true|Interface ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A friendly name or description for the interface or VLAN (max length 128 characters).|
|» subnet|body|string \| null|false|The network that this L3 interface is on, in CIDR notation (ex. 10.1.1.0/24).|
|» switchPortId|body|string \| null|false|Switch Port ID when in Routed mode (IOS XE firmware 17.18 or higher required)|
|» interfaceIp|body|string \| null|false|The IP address that will be used for Layer 3 routing on this VLAN or subnet. This cannot be the same         as the device management IP.|
|» mtu|body|integer \| null|false|The interface MTU. Applies to native switch layer 3 interfaces, including VLAN and routed modes.|
|» multicastRouting|body|string|false|Enable multicast support if, multicast routing between VLANs is required. Options are:         'disabled', 'enabled' or 'IGMP snooping querier'. Default is 'disabled'.|
|» vlanId|body|integer \| null|false|The VLAN this L3 interface is on. VLAN must be between 1 and 4094.|
|» defaultGateway|body|string|false|The next hop for any traffic that isn't going to a directly connected subnet or over a static route.         This IP address must exist in a subnet with a L3 interface. Required if this is the first IPv4 interface.|
|» ospfSettings|body|object|false|The OSPF routing settings of the interface.|
|» » area|body|string|false|The OSPF area to which this interface should belong. Can be either 'disabled' or the identifier of an           existing OSPF area. Defaults to 'disabled'.|
|» » cost|body|integer|false|The path cost for this interface. Defaults to 1, but can be increased up to 65535           to give lower priority.|
|» » isPassiveEnabled|body|boolean|false|When enabled, OSPF will not run on the interface, but the subnet will still be advertised.|
|» » networkType|body|string|false|OSPF network type|
|» ipv6|body|object|false|The IPv6 settings of the interface.|
|» » assignmentMode|body|string \| null|false|The IPv6 assignment mode for the interface. Can be either 'eui-64' or 'static'.|
|» » prefix|body|string \| null|false|The IPv6 prefix of the interface. Required if IPv6 object is included.|
|» » address|body|string \| null|false|The IPv6 address of the interface. Required if assignmentMode is 'static'. Must not be included if           assignmentMode is 'eui-64'.|
|» » gateway|body|string|false|The IPv6 default gateway of the interface. Required if prefix is defined and this is the first           interface with IPv6 configured.|
|» vrf|body|object|false|The VRF settings of the interface. Requires IOS XE 17.18 or higher|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the VRF this interface belongs to.|
|» loopback|body|object|false|The loopback settings of the interface.|
|» bidirectionalForwardingDetection|body|object|false|BFD configuration for the L3 interface.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether BFD is enabled on the L3 interface.|
|» » intervalInterface|body|object|false|BFD interval configuration for the L3 interface.|
|» » » msecs|body|integer \| null|false|BFD transmit interval in milliseconds.|
|» » » minRx|body|integer \| null|false|Minimum BFD receive interval in milliseconds.|
|» » » multiplier|body|integer \| null|false|BFD detection multiplier.|

|» multicastRouting|IGMP snooping querier|
|» multicastRouting|disabled|
|» multicastRouting|enabled|
|» » networkType|broadcast|
|» » networkType|point-to-point|

|» start|string|false|none|The starting IP address of the reserved IP range|
|» end|string|false|none|The ending IP address of the reserved IP range|

|» ip|string|false|none|The IP address of the client which has fixed IP address assigned to it|
|dhcpDefaultRouterIps|string|false|none|The DHCP default router IPs for the DHCP server running on the switch stack interface|
|dhcpDomainName|string \| null|false|none|The DHCP domain name for the DHCP server running on the switch stack interface|


```json
          "enabled": false
        }
      }

        "voiceSgtId": 1234
      },
      "failedAuthVlanId": 100,
      "failedAuthGroupPolicyId": "1234",
      "failedAuthSgtId": 1284392014819,

        "enabled": false,
        "timeout": 24
      },

        "mode": "Open"
      },
      "preAuthenticationGroupPolicyId": "1234"
    },
    "guestPortBouncing": false,
    "radiusTestingEnabled": false,
    "radiusCoaSupportEnabled": false,
    "radiusAccountingEnabled": true,
    "radiusAccountingServers": [
      {
        "serverId": "2",
        "organizationRadiusServerId": "42",
        "host": "1.2.3.4",
        "port": 22,
```
```bash
        "secret": "secret",
        "radsec": {
          "enabled": true
        }
      }
    ],
    "radiusGroupAttribute": "11",
    "hostMode": "Single-Host",
    "accessPolicyType": "Hybrid authentication",
    "increaseAccessSpeed": false,
    "guestVlanId": 100,

    },
```

## Create a switch stack

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkSwitchStack"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/switch/stacks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "A cool stack",
    "serials": [
      "QBZY-XWVU-TSRQ",
      "QBAB-CDEF-GHIJ"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/switch/stacks`

Create a switch stack

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "A cool stack",
  "serials": [
    "QBZY-XWVU-TSRQ",
    "QBAB-CDEF-GHIJ"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-switch-stack-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new stack|
|» serials|body|[string]|true|An array of switch serials to be added into the new stack|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "8473",
  "name": "A cool stack",
  "serials": [
    "QBZY-XWVU-TSRQ",
    "QBAB-CDEF-GHIJ"
  ],
  "workflowId": "8473"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-switch-stack-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-switch-stack-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|ID of the Switch stack|
|name|string|false|none|The name af the new stack|
|serials|[string]|false|none|An array of switch serials added to the stack|
|workflowId|string|false|none|ID of the workflow|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: switch:config:write )
</aside>

## Update a switch stack

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkSwitchStack"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/switch/stacks/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "A cool stack",
    "members": [
      {
        "serial": "QBZY-XWVU-TSRQ"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /networks/{networkId}/switch/stacks/{switchStackId}`

Update a switch stack. At least one of 'name' or 'members' must be provided. If 'members' is provided, it replaces the entire stack membership.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "A cool stack",
  "members": [
    {
      "serial": "QBZY-XWVU-TSRQ"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-switch-stack-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|switchStackId|path|string|true|Switch stack ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the switch stack|
|» members|body|[object]|false|The complete list of switches that should be in the stack. Minimum 2 and maximum 8 members. Omitting this field leaves stack membership unchanged.|
|» » serial|body|string|true|Serial number of a switch to include in the stack|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "8473",
  "name": "A cool stack",
  "serials": [
    "QBZY-XWVU-TSRQ",
    "QBAB-CDEF-GHIJ"
  ],
  "isMonitorOnly": false,
  "virtualMac": "00:18:0a:4f:21:19",
  "members": [
    {
      "serial": "QBZY-XWVU-TSRQ",
      "name": "switch 1",
      "model": "C9300-24T",
      "mac": "00:18:0a:00:00:09",
      "role": "active"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-switch-stack-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="update-a-switch-stack-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|none|ID of the switch stack|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the switch stack|
|serials|[string]|false|none|Serial numbers of the switches in the switch stack. Minimum 2 and maximum 8 serials.|
|isMonitorOnly|boolean|false|none|Whether the switch stack contains monitor-only switches.|
|virtualMac|string|false|none|The virtual MAC address of the switch stack|
|members|[object]|false|none|Members of the switch stack. Minimum 2 and maximum 8 members.|
|» serial|string|false|none|Serial number of the device|
|» name|string|false|none|Name of the device|
|» model|string|false|none|Model of the device|
|» mac|string|false|none|MAC address of the device|
|» role|string|false|none|Role of the device in the stack. Possible values are 'active', 'member', and 'standby'.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|active|
|» role|member|
|» role|standby|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: switch:config:write )
</aside>

## Create a layer 3 interface for a switch stack

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkSwitchStackRoutingInterface"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/switch/stacks/string/routing/interfaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "L3 interface",
    "mode": "vlan",
    "subnet": "192.168.1.0/24",
    "switchPortId": "1",
    "interfaceIp": "192.168.1.2",
    "mtu": 1500,
    "multicastRouting": "disabled",
    "vlanId": 100,
    "defaultGateway": "192.168.1.1",
    "ospfSettings": {
      "area": "0",
      "cost": 1,
      "isPassiveEnabled": true,
      "networkType": "broadcast"
    },
    "ipv6": {
      "assignmentMode": "static",
      "prefix": "2001:db8::/32",
      "address": "2001:db8::1",
      "gateway": "2001:db8::2"
    },
    "vrf": {
      "name": "Blue"
    },
    "bidirectionalForwardingDetection": {
      "enabled": true,
      "intervalInterface": {
        "msecs": 100,
        "minRx": 75,
        "multiplier": 5
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{networkId}/switch/stacks/{switchStackId}/routing/interfaces`

Create a layer 3 interface for a switch stack

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "L3 interface",
  "mode": "vlan",
  "subnet": "192.168.1.0/24",
  "switchPortId": "1",
  "interfaceIp": "192.168.1.2",
  "mtu": 1500,
  "multicastRouting": "disabled",
  "vlanId": 100,
  "defaultGateway": "192.168.1.1",
  "ospfSettings": {
    "area": "0",
    "cost": 1,
    "isPassiveEnabled": true,
    "networkType": "broadcast"
  },
  "ipv6": {
    "assignmentMode": "static",
    "prefix": "2001:db8::/32",
    "address": "2001:db8::1",
    "gateway": "2001:db8::2"
  },
  "vrf": {
    "name": "Blue"
  },
  "bidirectionalForwardingDetection": {
    "enabled": true,
    "intervalInterface": {
      "msecs": 100,
      "minRx": 75,
      "multiplier": 5
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-layer-3-interface-for-a-switch-stack-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|networkId|path|string|true|Network ID|
|switchStackId|path|string|true|Switch stack ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A friendly name or description for the interface or VLAN (max length 128 characters).|
|» mode|body|string|false|L3 Interface mode, can be one of 'vlan', 'routed', 'loopback', or 'oob_management'. Default is 'vlan'. IOS XE firmware 17.18 or higher is required for 'routed' mode; IOS XE firmware 26.1.2 or higher is required for 'oob_management' mode.|
|» subnet|body|string \| null|false|The network that this L3 interface is on, in CIDR notation (ex. 10.1.1.0/24).|
|» switchPortId|body|string \| null|false|Switch Port ID when in Routed mode (IOS XE firmware 17.18 or higher required)|
|» interfaceIp|body|string \| null|false|The IP address that will be used for Layer 3 routing on this VLAN or subnet. This cannot be the same         as the device management IP.|
|» mtu|body|integer \| null|false|The interface MTU. Applies to native switch layer 3 interfaces, including VLAN and routed modes.|
|» multicastRouting|body|string|false|Enable multicast support if, multicast routing between VLANs is required. Options are:         'disabled', 'enabled' or 'IGMP snooping querier'. Default is 'disabled'.|
|» vlanId|body|integer \| null|false|The VLAN this L3 interface is on. VLAN must be between 1 and 4094.|

## Update a layer 3 interface for a switch stack

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkSwitchStackRoutingInterface"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/switch/stacks/string/routing/interfaces/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "L3 interface",
    "subnet": "192.168.1.0/24",
    "switchPortId": "1",
    "interfaceIp": "192.168.1.2",
    "mtu": 1500,
    "multicastRouting": "disabled",
    "vlanId": 100,
    "defaultGateway": "192.168.1.1",
    "ospfSettings": {
      "area": "0",
      "cost": 1,
      "isPassiveEnabled": true,
      "networkType": "broadcast"
    },
    "ipv6": {
      "assignmentMode": "static",
      "prefix": "2001:db8::/32",
      "address": "2001:db8::1",
      "gateway": "2001:db8::2"
    },
    "vrf": {
      "name": "Blue"
    },
    "bidirectionalForwardingDetection": {
      "enabled": true,
      "intervalInterface": {
        "msecs": 100,
        "minRx": 75,
        "multiplier": 5
      }
    }
  }'
```

## Returns the total PoE power draw for all switch ports in the organization over the requested timespan (by default the last 24 hours)

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationSummarySwitchPowerHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/summary/switch/power/history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/summary/switch/power/history`

Returns the total PoE power draw for all switch ports in the organization over the requested timespan (by default the last 24 hours). The returned array is a newest-first list of intervals. The time between intervals depends on the requested timespan with 20 minute intervals used for timespans up to 1 day, 4 hour intervals used for timespans up to 2 weeks, and 1 day intervals for timespans larger than 2 weeks.

<h3 id="returns-the-total-poe-power-draw-for-all-switch-ports-in-the-organization-over-the-requested-timespan-by-default-the-last-24-hours-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 186 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 186 days. The default is 1 day.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "ts": "2021-06-20T01:00:00.000Z",
    "draw": 5.4321
  }
]
```

## Returns the counts of all active ports for the requested timespan, grouped by speed

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationSwitchPortsOverview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/switch/ports/overview \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/switch/ports/overview`

Returns the counts of all active ports for the requested timespan, grouped by speed. An active port is a port that at any point during the timeframe is observed to be connected to a responsive device and isn't configured to be disabled. For a port that is observed at multiple speeds during the timeframe, it will be counted at the highest speed observed. The number of inactive ports, and the total number of ports are also provided. Only ports on switches online during the timeframe will be represented and a port is only guaranteed to be present if its switch was online for at least 6 hours of the timeframe.

<h3 id="returns-the-counts-of-all-active-ports-for-the-requested-timespan-grouped-by-speed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 186 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be greater than or equal to 12 hours and be less than or equal to 186 days. The default is 1 day.|

```json
}
```

## Update an Organizations Sentry Policies using the provided list

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationSmSentryPoliciesAssignments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/sm/sentry/policies/assignments \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "networkId": "N_24329156",
        "policies": [
          {
            "policyId": "1284392014819",
            "smNetworkId": "N_24329156",
            "scope": "withAny",
            "tags": [
              "tag1",
              "tag2"
            ],
            "groupPolicyId": "1284392014819"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organizationId}/sm/sentry/policies/assignments`

Update an Organizations Sentry Policies using the provided list. Sentry Policies are ordered in descending order of priority (i.e. highest priority at the bottom, this is opposite the Dashboard UI). Policies not present in the request will be deleted.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "networkId": "N_24329156",
      "policies": [
        {
          "policyId": "1284392014819",
          "smNetworkId": "N_24329156",
          "scope": "withAny",
          "tags": [
            "tag1",
            "tag2"
          ],
          "groupPolicyId": "1284392014819"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organizations-sentry-policies-using-the-provided-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Organization ID|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» items|body|[object]|true|Sentry Group Policies for the Organization keyed by Network Id|
|» » networkId|body|string|true|The Id of the Network|
|» » policies|body|[object]|false|Array of Sentry Group Policies for the Network|
|» » » policyId|body|string|false|The Sentry Policy Id, if updating an existing Sentry Policy|
|» » » smNetworkId|body|string|true|The Id of the Systems Manager Network|

## Returns a historical log of all commands

<a id="opIdgetDeviceSensorCommands"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/devices/string/sensor/commands \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /devices/{serial}/sensor/commands`

Returns a historical log of all commands

<h3 id="returns-a-historical-log-of-all-commands-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serial|path|string|true|Serial|
|operations|query|[string]|false|Optional parameter to filter commands by operation. Allowed values are disableDownstreamPower, enableDownstreamPower, cycleDownstreamPower, and refreshData.|
|perPage|query|integer|false|The number of entries per page returned. Acceptable range is 3 - 1000. Default is 10.|
|startingAfter|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the start of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|endingBefore|query|string|false|A token used by the server to indicate the end of the page. Often this is a timestamp or an ID but it is not limited to those. This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|
|sortOrder|query|string|false|Sorted order of entries. Order options are 'ascending' and 'descending'. Default is 'descending'.|
|t0|query|string|false|The beginning of the timespan for the data. The maximum lookback period is 30 days from today.|
|t1|query|string|false|The end of the timespan for the data. t1 can be a maximum of 30 days after t0.|
|timespan|query|number(float)|false|The timespan for which the information will be fetched. If specifying timespan, do not specify parameters t0 and t1. The value must be in seconds and be less than or equal to 30 days. The default is 30 days.|

|---|---|

|sortOrder|descending|

|» » » » quality|body|string|false|Alerting threshold as a qualitative PM2.5 level.|
|» » » noise|body|object|false|Noise threshold. 'ambient' must be provided.|
|» » » » ambient|body|object|true|Ambient noise threshold. One of 'level' or 'quality' must be provided.|

|» » » apparentPower|body|object|false|Apparent power threshold. 'draw' must be provided.|

|» » » powerFactor|body|object|false|Power factor threshold. 'percentage' must be provided.|

|» » » current|body|object|false|Electrical current threshold. 'level' must be provided.|

## Updates a sensor alert profile for a network.

<a id="opIdupdateNetworkSensorAlertsProfile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/sensor/alerts/profiles/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My Sensor Alert Profile",
    "schedule": {
      "id": "5"
    },
    "conditions": [
      {
        "metric": "temperature",
        "threshold": {
          "temperature": {
            "celsius": 20.5,
            "fahrenheit": 70,
            "quality": "good"
          },
          "humidity": {
            "relativePercentage": 65,
            "quality": "inadequate"
          },
          "water": {
            "present": true
          },
          "door": {
            "open": true
          },
          "tvoc": {
            "concentration": 400,
            "quality": "poor"
          },
          "co2": {
            "concentration": 400,
            "quality": "poor"
          },
          "pm25": {
            "concentration": 90,
            "quality": "fair"
          },
          "noise": {
            "ambient": {
              "level": 120,
              "quality": "poor"
            }
          },
          "indoorAirQuality": {
            "score": 80,
            "quality": "fair"
          },
          "realPower": {
            "draw": 14.1
          },
          "apparentPower": {
            "draw": 17.2
          },
          "powerFactor": {
            "percentage": 81
          },
          "current": {
            "draw": 0.14
          },
          "voltage": {
            "level": 119.5
          },
          "frequency": {
            "level": 58.8
          },
          "upstreamPower": {
            "outageDetected": true
          }
        },
        "direction": "above",
        "duration": 60
      }
    ],
    "recipients": {
      "emails": [
        "miles@meraki.com"
      ],
      "smsNumbers": [
        "+15555555555"
      ],
      "httpServerIds": [
        "aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZXhhbXBsZS5jb20vd2ViaG9va3M="
      ]
    },
    "serials": [
      "Q234-ABCD-0001",
      "Q234-ABCD-0002",
      "Q234-ABCD-0003"
    ],
    "includeSensorUrl": true,
    "message": "Check with Miles on what to do."
  }'
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/sensor/readings/history`

<h3 id="return-all-reported-readings-from-sensors-in-a-given-timespan-sorted-by-timestamp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

```json
      "key": {
        "created": true
```

## Generates an API key for an identity

<a id="opIdgenerateAdministeredIdentitiesMeApiKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/administered/identities/me/api/keys/generate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /administered/identities/me/api/keys/generate`

Generates an API key for an identity. For users who have access to more than one organization, the change will take up to five minutes to propagate. If one of the organizations is currently under maintenance, the change may not propagate fully until after the maintenance has been completed.

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "key": "1284392014819"
}
```

<h3 id="generates-an-api-key-for-an-identity-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Successful operation|Inline|

<h3 id="generates-an-api-key-for-an-identity-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|string|false|none|API key in plaintext. This value will not be accessible outside of key generation|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
meraki_api_key, bearerAuth
</aside>


`POST /administered/identities/me/api/keys/{suffix}/revoke`

<h1 id="meraki-dashboard-api-campusgateway">campusGateway</h1>

## Create a cluster and add campus gateways to it

<a id="opIdcreateNetworkCampusGatewayCluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/networks/string/campusGateway/clusters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Cisco-Meraki-API-Key: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "North Campus",
    "uplinks": [
      {
        "interface": "man1",
        "vlan": 5,
        "addresses": [
          {
            "assignmentMode": "static",
            "protocol": "ipv4",
            "gateway": "1.2.3.5",
            "subnetMask": "255.255.255.0"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "tunnels": [
      {
        "uplink": {
          "interface": "man1"
        },
        "interface": "tun1",
        "vlan": 6,
        "addresses": [
          {
            "protocol": "ipv4",
            "gateway": "2.3.5.6",
            "subnetMask": "255.255.255.0"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "nameservers": {
      "addresses": [
        "8.8.8.8",
        "8.8.4.4"
      ]
    },
    "portChannels": [
      {
        "name": "Port-channel1",
        "vlan": 25,
        "allowedVlans": "10-20"
      }
    ],
    "devices": [
      {
        "serial": "Q234-ABCD-0001",
        "uplinks": [
          {
            "interface": "man1",
            "addresses": [
              {
                "protocol": "ipv4",
                "address": "5.1.2.3"
              }
            ]
          }
        ],
        "tunnels": [
          {
            "interface": "tun1",
            "addresses": [
              {
                "protocol": "ipv4",
                "address": "6.2.6.7"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "notes": "This cluster is for New York Office"
  }'
```

This parameter should not be defined by client applications. The link for the first, last, prev, or next page in the HTTP Link header should define it.|

## Moves a license to a different organization (coterm only)

<a id="opIdmoveOrganizationLicensingCotermLicenses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.meraki.com/api/v1/organizations/string/licensing/coterm/licenses/move \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "destination": {
      "organizationId": "123",
      "mode": "addDevices"
    },
    "licenses": [
      {
        "key": "Z2AA-BBBB-CCCC",
        "counts": [
          {
            "model": "MR Enterprise",
            "count": 5
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```
